notes: Same written form as 開く ひらく. あく is a thing opening on its own, a door, a shop. 開ける あける is you opening it.
sentence: 次の駅で右のドアが開きます。
mnemonic: 門 a gate with the bar lifted clean out of it and nobody's hand anywhere near. The train stops and the right-hand doors go by themselves: あく.
sentence_meaning: Doors on the right side will open at the next stop.

notes: Written exactly like 開く あく. Only what's around it tells you which. ひらく is spreading something open: a book, an umbrella, an event.
sentence: 32ページを開いてください。
mnemonic: The same gate as あく, except this time it's your hands on the bar. Page thirty-two, thumb into the middle, and the whole book comes apart flat: ひらく.
sentence_meaning: Please open to page 32.
A lot of food was left over.
mnemonic: 歹 bare bones with blades stacked up beside them. Whatever is still on the table once everybody has finished. Far too much of it, as usual: のこる.
meaning: to remain, to be left over
sentence: 料理がたくさん残りました。
notes: 残す のこす is leaving something behind on purpose.
答え こたえ is the answer itself.
sentence: 先生の質問に答えます。
sentence_meaning: I will answer the teacher's question.
mnemonic: 竹 bamboo strips with 合 the matching half fitted up against them. An answer is the piece that fits the question, and the teacher is waiting: こたえる.
忄 a heart with 布 a cloth thrown over it, hiding. Doesn't matter how small the dog is or whose it is. You're already behind someone: こわい.
sentence_meaning: I'm scared of dogs.
notes: Does both jobs: the person who is afraid, and the thing that is frightening.
sentence: 私は犬が怖いです。

mnemonic: One harvest carried in, then another, and you count them off. Five of them in Korea before you looked up: 5年, ごねん.
sentence_meaning: I was in South Korea for five years.
sentence: 韓国に5年いました。
notes: Same kanji as 年 とし. ねん is the one that sits behind a number and counts.

sentence: 新しい年が始まりました。
notes: Same kanji as 年 ねん, which only counts. とし is the year as a thing in itself, the reading you already met in 毎年 まいとし.
sentence_meaning: A new year has started.
mnemonic: The same harvest as ねん, except nobody is counting it. A whole new one has just started and it's still completely empty: とし.

sentence_meaning: I got a good grade on the test.
mnemonic: 耳 an ear with 又 a hand closed round it. Old soldiers took ears off the field to prove the count. You took a good mark off that test: とる.
sentence: テストでいい点を取った。

mnemonic: 全 a king under one roof, and everything under that roof with him. You told him the lot, nothing held back at all: すべて.
sentence_meaning: I told him everything.
notes: 全部 ぜんぶ is the everyday spoken one; 全て leans a little more written.
sentence: 彼に全てのことを伝えた。

notes: Stronger than English "help". It stretches all the way to rescuing and saving a life. 助かる たすかる is being on the receiving end of it.
sentence: 彼女は病気の犬を助けた。
sentence_meaning: She helped a sick dog.
mnemonic: 力 power stuck on the right-hand side. An extra shoulder put under the load. The dog was ill in a ditch and she carried it home: たすける.
状 the shape a thing has taken, with 犬 a dog in it, and 況 water running past. Look at the state of it. Nobody is setting off in this: じょうきょう.
sentence_meaning: It will be difficult to depart in these conditions.
sentence: この状況では出発は難しいです。
もう一度、予約を確認した。
notes: 確認する is one of the most common words in Japanese office life. Checking a thing before it goes wrong.
sentence_meaning: I confirmed my reservation one more time.
mnemonic: 確 a 石 stone, solid enough to be sure of, and 認 words you finally accept. You check the booking one more time anyway: かくにん.

sentence: 電気が消えているので、田中さんは部屋にいないでしょう。
notes: 消す けす is you turning it off; 消える is it going out. Same split as 出る and 出す.
sentence_meaning: The light is off, so Tanaka-san must not be in this room.
mnemonic: 氵 water on the left, wearing something away until there's nothing there. The light is off and the room has gone with it: きえる.

sentence: 彼女の髪はとても長い。
notes: Length in space or in time. The same kanji reads ちょう in 社長 しゃちょう, a company head.
sentence_meaning: Her hair is very long.
mnemonic: Long hair on an old figure, drawn flowing all the way down the character. Hers goes past where the drawing stops: ながい.

meaning: to be surprised, to be astonished
sentence_meaning: I was surprised by a loud voice on the street in the middle of the night.
mnemonic: 馬 a horse underneath the whole thing, and something has just gone off beside it. A shout in an empty street at two in the morning and you come off the ground: おどろく.
sentence: 夜中に道で大きな声がして、驚きました。
腕を回してください。
notes: Also means skill. 腕がいい is 'good at it', the way English says a safe pair of hands.
mnemonic: The 月 that means flesh, with a shape for bending sat beside it. The physio wants it all the way round, both directions: うで.
sentence_meaning: Please rotate your arm.

mnemonic: 以 the marker that fixes a boundary, and 外 everything sat outside it. Every day on the bike, and rain filed on the far side of the line: いがい.
sentence_meaning: I go to school by bicycle except on rainy days.
sentence: 私は雨の日以外は自転車で学校に行く。
notes: Same 以 as 以上 いじょう. 以上 counts from a point upward; 以外 cuts one thing out and keeps the rest. Same reading as 意外 いがい, unexpected, which is a different word entirely.

sentence_meaning: I'm at a loss because I lost my cell phone.
mnemonic: 木 a tree boxed inside 囗 four walls, with nowhere left to grow. Phone gone, every number in it, and you're standing there doing nothing: こまる.
meaning: to be at a loss, to be troubled
sentence: ケータイをなくして困っています。
実家を4年間離れていました。
sentence_meaning: I was away from my parents' house for 4 years.
mnemonic: 隹 a small bird on the right, gone off the branch and not coming back to it. Four years away from your parents' house before you saw it again: はなれる.
meaning: to be separated, to be apart

notes: Turns up in a huge number of set phrases: 気をつけて be careful, 気にしないで don't worry about it.
sentence: 旅行に行く気があるか彼女に聞かれました。
sentence_meaning: She asked if I was willing to travel.
mnemonic: Steam coming off something, the same 気 that sits in 元気. On its own it's whatever you've got rising in you. And she wants to know if any of it is for travelling: き.

sentence: 彼に手紙を書きました。
notes: 描く かく is the same sound for drawing a picture. Writing is 書く.
mnemonic: 聿 a hand gripping a brush, sat straight down on the thing it's marking. A whole letter to him, by hand, and then you had to post it: かく.
sentence_meaning: I wrote him a letter.

sentence: この部屋は光がたくさん入って、いいね。
notes: 光る ひかる is the verb, to shine.
sentence_meaning: It’s nice how much light comes into this room, isn’t it?
mnemonic: A figure on 儿 legs with brightness coming off the top of its head. Whoever built this room pointed it the right way, the stuff pours in: ひかり.

sentence: 彼は毎晩3キロ走っています。
sentence_meaning: Every night he runs three kilometers.
mnemonic: 土 the earth up top with legs driving away underneath it. Three kilometres of it, every night, in the dark, without being asked: はしる.

sentence: 彼は最後まで戦ったよ。
mnemonic: 戈 a halberd stood up on the right-hand side, and somebody still holding it. 最後 the very last moment, and he had not put it down: たたかう.
sentence_meaning: He fought to the very end.

sentence: 余りは次回使いましょう。
notes: Same word as the kana あまり 'not very'. With a negative it means there isn't much of something, and this is the something.
mnemonic: A roof with whatever didn't get used stacked underneath it. Too much fabric, too much batter, and none of it thrown away: あまり.
sentence_meaning: Let's use the left-over portion next time.
I ate all that was in the lunchbox.
mnemonic: 全 the whole thing and 部 every section of it accounted for. The lunchbox goes back empty, not most of it, all of it: ぜんぶ.
sentence: お弁当を全部食べました。
notes: The everyday spoken one. 全て すべて is the same idea, a shade more written.

sentence: その瞬間、猫が跳び出しました。
notes: 間 reads かん here, the same as in 時間 じかん.
mnemonic: 目 an eye on the left, open exactly as long as a blink, and 間 the gap it makes. That's how much warning you got before the cat went: しゅんかん.
sentence_meaning: At that instant, the cat ran out.

sentence: この文法の説明は良く分かりません。
sentence_meaning: I don't really understand the explanation of this grammar.
mnemonic: 説 words worked at until they come loose, and 明 the sun and moon making it bright. Neither of those has happened to this grammar page: せつめい.

sentence_meaning: Let's decide the time of the meeting.
mnemonic: 氵 water on the left, cut a channel and it only runs one way after that. Pick the time for the meeting and everyone else's day pours into it: きめる.
sentence: 会議の時間を決めましょう。
notes: 決まる きまる is it being decided; 決める is somebody deciding it.

sentence: そのパーティーに女性は何人来ますか。
notes: The polite one. Bare 女 おんな can sound blunt about a person; 女性 never does.
mnemonic: 女 a woman with 性 a 忄 heart and 生 a life beside her, the whole person, not just the label. This is the word you use in front of people: じょせい.
sentence_meaning: How many women are coming to that party?

notes: The humble version of 受ける and もらう: it lowers you, not them. It's also the いただきます said before eating.
sentence: お客様にお菓子を頂いた。
sentence_meaning: A customer gave me some snacks.
mnemonic: 頂 is the very top of a thing, 頁 a head with the crown marked on it. You take the sweets with both hands and your own head goes down: いただく.

sentence: あそこに敵がひそんでいる。
sentence_meaning: The enemy is lurking there.
mnemonic: 攵 the strike radical stood on the right, waiting. Somebody is behind that wall and they are not on your side: てき.

sentence: 近所で盗難事件が起きました。
notes: Same word as 起きる "to get up". Events use it too: a thing rises up and happens.
sentence_meaning: Some burglaries occurred in the neighborhood.
mnemonic: 走 running with 己 yourself behind it. Something stands up out of nowhere. Three break-ins on your own street, and none of them were there last week: おきる.

meaning: to get up, to get out of bed
sentence_meaning: I get up at six o'clock every morning.
mnemonic: The same standing-up as the one events do, only this time it's you. Six o'clock, every single morning, upright before you've decided to be: おきる.
notes: Same word as 起きる "to occur". Careful with 怒る おこる, to get angry, one vowel apart.
sentence: 私は毎朝6時に起きます。

sentence_meaning: My bag fell down there.
mnemonic: 艹 grass and 氵 water up at the top of the character, both on their way down. Your bag goes off the rack and lands somewhere under the seat: おちる.
notes: 落とす おとす is you dropping it; 落ちる is it falling by itself.
sentence: 荷物が下に落ちてしまいました。

mnemonic: 口 a knee drawn on top of the foot underneath it. His go on for ever, trousers never fit him off the peg: あし.
sentence_meaning: He has long legs.
sentence: 彼は足が長い。
notes: Covers the whole thing, leg and foot together. Japanese doesn't split them the way English does.

mnemonic: The hotels cost double over the long weekend. それに. And on top of that, every single place is heaving. One complaint stacked straight onto another.
sentence_meaning: Hotel fares are expensive during extended weekends. In addition, it's crowded everywhere.
notes: Piles a second point onto the first. そして just adds the next thing; それで says the first caused the second.
sentence: 連休はホテル代が高いです。それに、どこも人が多いです。

sentence_meaning: We will leave before you then.
mnemonic: 先 a figure striding out in front on 儿 legs, the same 先 as 先生. You're off now and they can catch up later: さきに.
notes: お先に失礼します is the standard line for leaving the office before your colleagues.
sentence: では、私たちは先に出発します。
彼女はまるで魔法にかかったみたいだ。
mnemonic: 魔 a demon crouched under the roof, and 法 water finding the one way down. She's behaving as though somebody set that loose on her: まほう.
sentence_meaning: She acts as if she is under a spell.

sentence: ピンクのセーターをずっと探しています。
sentence_meaning: I've been looking for a pink sweater for a while.
mnemonic: 扌 a hand reaching right down into somewhere deep and feeling about. Every shop, every week, still no pink jumper: さがす.

sentence_meaning: Kids were making a racket in the train.
mnemonic: 子 a child with 供 more of them along for the ride. Not one of them on the whole carriage is sitting still: こども.
notes: Same 子 as 子 こ. 子供 is the ordinary standalone word for a child.
sentence: 電車で子供が騒いでいた。

mnemonic: 奴 a servant sat on top of 心 the heart, and the heart underneath is doing all the work. She lied and he has gone quiet in a way that isn't quiet: おこる.
sentence_meaning: He was angry because she lied.
notes: One vowel from 起きる おきる, to get up, and identical in sound to 起こる おこる, to happen. Also covers telling someone off, not just being cross.
sentence: 彼女が嘘をついたので、彼は怒った。

mnemonic: 笑 bamboo bent double and 顔 a face to put it on. Not the laugh itself, the face doing it. And on a baby it finishes you: えがお.
sentence_meaning: The baby's smile is cute.
notes: 笑う わらう is the verb. 笑顔 is the face, and it's the word you'd use for a photo.
sentence: 赤ちゃんの笑顔が可愛い。

mnemonic: 先 the one out in front, with 輩 a row of carts strung out behind. They joined a year before you and that never stops counting: せんぱい.
sentence_meaning: Did you get a text from your senior?
sentence: 先輩からメール来た？
notes: 後輩 こうはい is the other end, anyone who joined after you. The pair runs your whole working life.

mnemonic: 糸 a thread that nobody has cut. Two full weeks of rain, one day joined onto the next, and no end showing: つづく.
sentence_meaning: Rainy days have continued for two weeks.
sentence: 雨の日が２週間も続いています。
notes: 続ける つづける is you keeping something going; 続く is it going on by itself.
そんなに is that much, over by them; あんなに is that much, over there.
sentence: こんなに面白い本は初めて読んだ。
mnemonic: こ- is the near one again, the same こ as これ. You're holding the book up so somebody can see how much you mean: こんなに.
sentence_meaning: It's the first time I read such an interesting book.

sentence: 変な音が聞こえます。
notes: Same kanji as 変わる かわる and 変える かえる, which are the verbs. 変 on its own is the adjective.
mnemonic: The same 変 as 変わる, one thing turning into another. But caught halfway, when it isn't either. Something in the wall is making a noise it shouldn't: へん.
sentence_meaning: I hear a strange sound.

sentence: 日本語の本を読みます。
mnemonic: 言 speech with 売 selling beside it. The words were written down to be handed on. You take them off the page in Japanese now: よむ.
sentence_meaning: I read a Japanese language book.

notes: Shares its 然 with 全然 ぜんぜん.
sentence: 彼女が怒るのも当然だ。
meaning: natural, as a matter of course
mnemonic: 当 landing squarely on the spot and 然 that being how it is. She was lied to. Of course she's angry. Where else was that going to land: とうぜん.
sentence_meaning: It's natural that she would be angry.

mnemonic: 情 what's going on inside a thing, and 報 a hand passing the news of it over. Everything about the hotel that isn't on the front page: じょうほう.
sentence_meaning: I'd like to know some information about the hotel.
notes: Shares its 情 with 表情 ひょうじょう, where the feeling shows on the outside instead.
sentence: 私はホテルの情報が知りたいです。

sentence_meaning: I found a new job.
mnemonic: 見 an eye on legs and 付 a hand fixing onto what it saw. Months of looking, and then a job. Spotted and taken hold of: みつける.
notes: You spotting it and taking hold. 見つかる みつかる is it being found, or you being caught.
sentence: 新しい仕事を見つけました。
少女は母親の手を握った。
notes: A written, slightly literary word. In speech you'd say 女の子 おんなのこ.
sentence_meaning: The girl clasped her mother's hand.
mnemonic: 少 a small amount of 女 woman, not grown yet. She reaches up and takes her mother's hand without looking: しょうじょ.

sentence_meaning: A terrible thing happened.
mnemonic: 大 big and 変 strange stuck together, a large amount of something going badly wrong. Whatever has happened, it isn't small: たいへん.
notes: Also does duty as 'very' in front of an adjective: 大変おいしい is very tasty. Same 変 as 変 へん.
sentence: 大変なことが起こりました。
彼はかなり英語が上手です。
notes: Stronger than ちょっと, softer than とても. It carries a small note of surprise.
mnemonic: More than you were expecting, less than you'd call fluent. He opens his mouth and you quietly adjust upwards: かなり.
sentence_meaning: He's pretty good at English.

mnemonic: A mark sitting below the line, the exact mirror of 上. Your purse has been under the desk the entire time you've been turning the house over: した.
sentence_meaning: My purse was under the desk.
notes: Same kanji as 下 もと. した is physically underneath. It also reads か and げ in compounds. 地下 ちか is underground.
sentence: 財布は机の下にあった。

notes: Same kanji as 下 した. した is under a desk; もと is under someone's authority, a boss, a professor, a rule.
sentence: 私はその教授の下で論文を書いたの。
mnemonic: The same mark below the line as した, except nothing is physically on top of you. You wrote the whole thesis in that professor's shadow: もと.
sentence_meaning: I wrote my thesis under that professor's supervision.

mnemonic: Ten minutes on the bike and you don't get to argue about it. かかる is the meter running: the thing costs whatever it costs.
sentence_meaning: It takes about 10 minutes by bicycle.
notes: Same sound as 掛かる かかる 'to hang', but this one is normally written in kana. 時間がかかる, お金がかかる.
sentence: 自転車で10分ぐらいかかります。
綺麗なカレンダーが掛かっていますね。
notes: 掛ける かける is you hanging it; 掛かる is it hanging. Same sound as the kana かかる, 'to take time'.
mnemonic: 扌 a hand at a peg, the same 掛 as 掛ける. But nobody's hand is on it now. The calendar is simply up there, being beautiful at you: かかる.
sentence_meaning: A beautiful calendar is hanging, isn't it?

notes: Same 度 as 今度 こんど. もう一度 もういちど is 'one more time'.
sentence: 一度、花見をしたことがあります。
sentence_meaning: I went flower viewing once before.
mnemonic: 一 one and 度 a single turn of the wheel. Flower viewing, exactly the one time, years ago, and you still bring it up: いちど.
完 everything finished off under 宀 one roof, and 全 the whole of it still there. The temple has not lost a single beam in a thousand years: かんぜん.
sentence_meaning: This old Buddhist temple still maintains its complete form.
sentence: この古い寺院は今でも完全な形を保っているんだ。
後ろを向いて。
notes: Same kanji as 後 あと 'after' and the ご in 今後. うしろ is the physical one.
sentence_meaning: Turn around.
mnemonic: The same 後 you already have as あと, but aimed at space instead of time. Not later, behind you. Turn round and look: うしろ.

sentence: 妹はすぐに泣く。
notes: Tears. 鳴く なく is the identical sound for the noise an animal makes.
sentence_meaning: My little sister cries easily.
mnemonic: 氵 water beside 立 somebody standing there. She hasn't moved and she hasn't said anything, and it's already coming down her face: なく.

sentence_meaning: The road is in a very bad state here.
mnemonic: 状 the shape a thing has taken, with 態 putting 心 a heart under it. Look at the state of this road, potholes the entire way along: じょうたい.
sentence: ここは道の状態がとても悪いです。
notes: Shares its 状 with 状況 じょうきょう. 状態 is the condition a thing is in; 状況 is the situation going on around it.

mnemonic: 関 a gate with the bar across it, and 係 a person tied onto a line running through. He isn't anywhere on that line. Nothing connects him to it: かんけい.
sentence_meaning: He has nothing to do with that incident.
sentence: 彼はその事件に関係がない。
notes: 関係ない is one of the most common phrases going: 'nothing to do with me'.

mnemonic: 向 the window that only faces one way, except now somebody has turned it. He puts both eyes on his boss and leaves them there: むける.
sentence_meaning: He stared with angry eyes at his superior.
meaning: to turn toward, to point at
sentence: 彼は上司に怒りの目を向けたんだよ。
notes: 向かう むかう is heading that way yourself; 向ける is aiming something else.
Same sound as 置く おく, 'to put'. 奥 is the depths of something. And 奥さん is somebody's wife.
sentence: はさみは机の奥にあった。
sentence_meaning: The scissors were at the back of the desk.
mnemonic: Something shut deep inside the frame with 大 spread across the bottom to keep it in. The scissors were at the very back of the drawer the whole time: おく.
車 a cart on the left, built light enough for one person to pull. You brace to lift the shoes and nearly put them through the ceiling: かるい.
sentence_meaning: These shoes are very light.
notes: Also light in the sense of not serious. 軽い風邪 is a mild cold.
sentence: この靴はとても軽い。

mnemonic: 辶 the road with 反 something turned over on it. Back the way you came, carrying the thing. The book goes into the library slot: かえす.
sentence_meaning: I returned the book to the library.
notes: Careful: 帰る かえる is you going home and 変える かえる is altering something. 返す is giving a thing back.
sentence: 図書館に本を返した。
雲の間から太陽が現れました。
sentence_meaning: The sun appeared between the clouds.
mnemonic: 王 a jewel with 見 an eye brought up to it. The instant a thing becomes visible. The cloud slides off and the sun is simply there: あらわれる.
疒 the sickness radical wrapped the whole way round it. One tooth, and it has taken over that entire side of your head: いたい.
sentence_meaning: My tooth hurts.
notes: Also what you shout when it happens. 痛い is the Japanese for 'ouch'.
sentence: 歯が痛いです。

notes: Usually has らしい or ようだ waiting later in the sentence.
sentence: 明日はどうやら雨らしいよ。
mnemonic: Nobody has confirmed a thing. But the forecast, the sky and the way your knee feels all agree. どうやら it's raining tomorrow.
sentence_meaning: Seems like it's going to rain tomorrow.

mnemonic: 灬 fire down at the bottom, and 点 is one single spot of it. Somebody has to go and put a light to the room: つける.
sentence_meaning: Please turn on the light.
sentence: 電気を点けてください。
notes: Same sound as 付ける つける. This one is for anything that lights up, lamps, switches, the telly. つく on its own is it coming on by itself.

sentence_meaning: I added a freebie.
mnemonic: 亻 a person and 寸 a hand, pressing one thing onto another. Not the light this time, a freebie slipped into the bag on top of the order: つける.
meaning: to attach, to set, to add
sentence: おまけを付けました。
notes: Same sound as 点ける つける, which is for lights. This is attaching anything to anything, and it is the same 付 as 見つける. 付く つく is it sticking to something on its own.

sentence_meaning: I doubted my ears for an instant.
mnemonic: 一 one 瞬 blink, the same 瞬 that sits in 瞬間. That is precisely how long you spent not believing your own ears: いっしゅん.
notes: 瞬間 しゅんかん is the moment itself; 一瞬 is 'for an instant', and behaves like an adverb.
sentence: 一瞬自分の耳を疑ったよ。

sentence_meaning: Is there anything you're hiding from me?
mnemonic: Whatever it was has gone round the far side of the hill where nobody can see it. Is there anything behind yours? Asked in the voice that already knows: かくす.
notes: 隠れる かくれる is you hiding yourself; 隠す is hiding something.
sentence: 僕に隠していることは無いですか。
明日の会議の準備をした。
sentence_meaning: I prepared for tomorrow's meeting.
mnemonic: 準 water levelled off flat, and 備 a person with everything laid out ready beside them. Tomorrow's meeting, the whole of it sorted tonight: じゅんび.

notes: Softens whatever comes after it. そろそろ帰ります is the polite way to announce you're going.
sentence: そろそろ始めましょうか。
mnemonic: Nobody has said anything, but people have started looking at the clock and gathering their coats. そろそろ. Shall we make a start, then?
sentence_meaning: It's about time to begin.
Calm down and listen to me.
mnemonic: 落ちる falling and 着く landing, bolted together. Everything that was up in the air comes down and stays down. Sit. Now listen: おちつく.
meaning: to calm down, to settle in
sentence: 私の話を落ち着いて聞いてください。
notes: Built straight out of 落ちる おちる. Also used of settling into a new place, and of a room that feels calm.

sentence: とても恥ずかしかった。
notes: Covers embarrassed and shy at once. The feeling, and the thing that causes it.
sentence_meaning: It was very embarrassing.
mnemonic: 耳 an ear sat over 心 the heart, because the ears are the part that gives you away. Both of them scarlet before you'd even finished the sentence: はずかしい.

sentence_meaning: Please ask me in case you don't understand.
mnemonic: 場 a place, the same 場 as 場所, with 合 things fitting together in it. The particular set of circumstances you find yourself in, stuck, in this case: ばあい.
sentence: 分からない場合は私に聞いてください。
両手でしっかり持って。
notes: Same word as しっかり "reliable". This one is about grip, the other is about a person.
sentence_meaning: Hold it firmly with both hands.
mnemonic: Both hands, and no daylight between your fingers. Whatever it is, it is not going to be the one that slips: しっかり.
The same grip as holding something in both hands, turned on a person instead. He's twenty-three and nothing has ever been dropped: しっかり.
sentence_meaning: He is reliable even though he is young.
sentence: 彼は若いのにしっかりしてるね。
notes: Same word as しっかり "tightly". Said of a person it means solid and dependable.
The hair on your head. 毛 け is hair anywhere else. Three かみ in the deck, told apart by the kanji: 髪 hair, 神 god, 紙 paper.
sentence: 昨日、髪を切りました。
sentence_meaning: I had my hair cut yesterday.
mnemonic: 髟 the long-hair radical spread right across the top of the character. All of it came off yesterday and nobody at work has said a word: かみ.

notes: Same sound as 下 もと, 'under the supervision of'. This one goes in front of a role: 元選手, a former player.
sentence: あの人は卓球の元選手です。
mnemonic: 元 is where a thing started, the same 元 as 元気. Stick it on the front of a job and it means that's where they started, and stopped: もと.
sentence_meaning: That person is a former table tennis player.

sentence: 彼は大金を得ましたよ。
notes: Formal. In speech もらう or 手に入れる do the same job.
sentence_meaning: He gained a lot of money.
mnemonic: 彳 the step radical with a hand and a prize on the right. You go out and you come back holding it. He came back holding rather a lot: える.

sentence_meaning: I'll go right away.
mnemonic: Not in a minute, not after this. You're already reaching for your coat while you're saying it: すぐ.
notes: Also does distance. すぐそこ is 'just over there'.
sentence: すぐ行きます。

notes: 月 reads げつ here, not つき as in 毎月 まいつき. Same 来 as 来年 らいねん.
sentence: 来月から大学生になります。
sentence_meaning: I'll be a college student starting next month.
mnemonic: 来 the crop not yet in, sat on 月 the moon. One more turn of it and you stop being a school pupil for good: らいげつ.

sentence_meaning: A long time ago this was an ocean.
mnemonic: Strokes stacked up over 日 the sun. Days piled behind you until you can't see past them. Stand here and it was all water once: むかし.
meaning: a long time ago, the old days
sentence: 昔、ここは海でした。

sentence_meaning: The station is near here.
mnemonic: 辶 the road with 斤 an axe on it. Close enough that one swing covers it. The station is round the corner, you'll hear the announcements: ちかい.
sentence: 駅はここから近いです。
notes: 最近 さいきん, 'recently', is this kanji doing the same job with time.

mnemonic: 動く moving, stopped just short of being a verb. Before you do anything at all, watch what the 相手 across from you is doing with their feet: うごき.
sentence_meaning: First, watch your opponent's moves.
sentence: まず相手の動きを見ましょう。
notes: The noun from 動く うごく. Uses 相手 あいて, the word for whoever is on the other side.

sentence: 彼はその絵をずっと見つめていたの。
notes: One of the 見 family: 見る is looking, 見える is being visible, 見つける is finding, 見つめる is not looking away.
mnemonic: 見 an eye that has landed on something and packed it in tight. He stood in front of that painting and did not move for forty minutes: みつめる.
sentence_meaning: He kept gazing at that painting the whole time.

mnemonic: 幸 the shape for a lucky escape. Nothing has happened, nothing has been won. You just have good friends and that turns out to be the whole thing: しあわせ.
sentence_meaning: I'm happy to have good friends.
notes: A settled, lasting happiness. 嬉しい うれしい is the sharp kind, about one particular thing.
sentence: 良い友達がいて私は幸せだ。

sentence_meaning: I clearly remember what happened at that time.
mnemonic: 記 words written down beside 己 yourself, and 憶 a 忄 heart holding the thought. Everything from back then is still filed, and still sharp: きおく.
sentence: 当時のことはしっかり記憶しているよ。
notes: The stored thing. 覚える おぼえる is the act of putting it there.
Same 反 as 返す かえす. Both are about a thing coming back at you.
sentence: 彼女は良い反応を示したわ。
mnemonic: 反 something turned back and 応 a 心 heart under a shelter answering it. You put a thing in front of her and it came straight back, warmly: はんのう.
sentence_meaning: She showed a good reaction.

mnemonic: 私 the one you already know, with たち piled on the end to make it more than one. Next month there'll be a certificate saying so: わたしたち.
sentence_meaning: We will get married next month.
sentence: 私たちは来月結婚します。
notes: たち pluralises people generally, 子供たち, 友達. Never used for objects.

sentence: とにかく現場へ行ってみましょう。
notes: Sweeps the argument aside and moves on to what you're actually going to do.
sentence_meaning: Anyway, let's go to the site.
mnemonic: Everyone has a theory and nobody has been outside. とにかく. Right, whatever the answer is, we're going down there to look.

notes: 勝手に means 'without asking anyone'. 勝手に決めた, decided it on his own.
sentence: 勝手なことばかり言わないでくれ。
sentence_meaning: Don't say self-centered things all the time.
mnemonic: 勝 winning with 手 a hand, playing every round for yourself and nobody else at the table. Enough of it now: かって.

notes: Does military attacks and verbal ones. 攻撃的 こうげきてき is 'aggressive' about a person.
sentence: 2003年にアメリカはイラクを攻撃した。
mnemonic: 攻 going at something with 攵 the strike radical, and 撃 a hand driving the whole weight down. It covers armies, and it covers what people do to each other in print: こうげき.
sentence_meaning: The United States attacked Iraq in 2003.

sentence: 窓を開けてください。
notes: The third of the set: 開く あく is it opening on its own, 開く ひらく is spreading something open, 開ける あける is you opening it.
mnemonic: 門 the gate again, and this time your hands are on the bar. The window doesn't slide itself. Somebody has to get up: あける.
sentence_meaning: Please open the window.

mnemonic: 黒 black with 犬 a dog underneath it, sat there not making a sound. He gets in, gets on with it, and you hear nothing all day: だまる.
sentence_meaning: He always works in silence.
meaning: to become silent, to shut one's mouth
sentence: 彼はいつも黙って仕事をします。
notes: 黙って means 'without saying anything'. It can be admiring or it can be an order.

sentence: 最近、仕事が忙しいです。
notes: Same 最 as 最初 and 最後. Covers 'recently' and 'these days' both.
sentence_meaning: Recently, I have been busy at work.
mnemonic: 最 the extreme end of something and 近 near. The closest bit of the past to where you're stood. Work has been like this for a few weeks now: さいきん.

sentence_meaning: The name tags were distributed to every member.
mnemonic: 全 the whole lot and 員 each 口 mouth on the list counted off. Every single person on the team got one, down to the reserves: ぜんいん.
notes: 全部 ぜんぶ is everything; 全員 is everybody. People take 員, things take 部.
sentence: チーム全員に名札が配られました。
自分の失敗を他人のせいにするな。
notes: Always for bad outcomes. For good ones it's おかげ, thanks to someone.
sentence_meaning: Don't blame others for your failure.
mnemonic: You dropped it, and within a second it's the floor's doing, or the light, or whoever handed it to you. せい is where the finger lands when it isn't pointing at you.
氵 water on the left with a hand reaching down into it and not touching anything. Nobody swims in that pond twice: ふかい.
sentence_meaning: That pond is very deep.
sentence: あの池はとても深い。
notes: Does depth and profundity both. 深い意味 is a deep meaning.

sentence_meaning: Please show me another book.
mnemonic: 刂 a blade cuts one card out of the deck and drops it face up, a different suit from everything else on the table. I would bet Sue swapped it: べつ.
notes: 別に べつに is this word plus に, and nearly always sits in a negative sentence. 別 on its own is just separate, or another one.
sentence: 別の本も見せてください。

mnemonic: 氵 a channel cut long before you turned up, and the water only goes one way now. The dates are on the calendar already. Ask Kim: a rule is a rule. きまる.
sentence_meaning: The travel dates have been set.
meaning: to be decided, to be set
sentence: 旅行の日程が決まりました。
notes: 決める きめる is somebody deciding. 決まる is it coming out decided, often with nobody visible doing it.

sentence: そこでしばらく休んでいます。
notes: Vague on purpose. Anything from a few minutes to a few years, and しばらくぶり is what you say after a long gap.
mnemonic: The landlady drops the bar across the door and sits back down. Nobody is leaving for a good while yet. She barred the lock: しばらく.
sentence_meaning: He's resting over there for a while.
meaning: for a while, for the time being

sentence_meaning: The Winter Olympics were held in Japan in 1998.
mnemonic: 行 the crossroads from above, closed off today for the race. Someone has to set out every cone, and shin one doing it: oh, cone, ow. おこなう.
sentence: １９９８年に日本で冬のオリンピックが行われました。
notes: Same 行 as 行く いく. 行く is going somewhere, 行う is putting the event on, and its reading is the odd one to hold on to.

mnemonic: 上 a mark sitting above the line. Leave the dough by the Aga, ruin the cloth over it, and by morning it has climbed the bowl on its own: あがる.
sentence_meaning: We went up to the second floor.
notes: 上げる あげる is you raising something. 上がる is it going up by itself: prices, temperature, or you to the next floor.
sentence: 私たちは２階に上がった。

sentence_meaning: They have a dog next door.
mnemonic: 阝 a mound on the left, and somebody else's garden behind it. Whatever they are cooking comes over the bank every evening, tuna rice again: となり.
notes: The one immediately beside you. 近く ちかく is loosely nearby.
sentence: 隣の家には犬がいます。

notes: The panel that swings, and a shade more literary than ドア. It is also the title page of a book.
sentence: 彼は扉を開けたんだ。
sentence_meaning: He opened the door.
mnemonic: 戸 a door with 非 stacked up behind it. It swings in harder than anyone expects. Your toe, then the beer, then the whole room going ah: とびら.

sentence_meaning: He has fat fingers.
mnemonic: 扌 a hand and 旨 the point of the thing, so this is what you point with. Reach in among the flowers and the sting lands on it first: you, bee. ゆび.
notes: Fingers and toes both. 足の指 あしのゆび is a toe.
sentence: 彼は指が太い。

mnemonic: 糸 a thread pulled into a knot and 果 the fruit a tree finally lets go of. Nobody wants the story of the match, only the number chalked up at the end: けっか.
sentence_meaning: I want to know the results of the game soon.
notes: その結果 is as a result, and 〜した結果 is what came of doing the thing.
sentence: 試合の結果を早く知りたい。

mnemonic: 与 is a thing going out of one hand and into another. She folds your fingers round it and the hall claps before you have even looked. Ah, ta. Eh? A ruler. あたえる.
sentence_meaning: That news gave him a great shock.
sentence: そのニュースは彼に大きなショックを与えた。
notes: Formal, and it takes the abstract objects: 影響を与える to have an influence, ショックを与える to give someone a shock. あげる is the everyday give.

mnemonic: 辶 the road radical under 首 a neck, the way running off wherever your head points. He knows this one so well the Michelin map stays in the glovebox: みち.
sentence_meaning: I know this road.
sentence: この道を知っています。
notes: Also the way of doing a thing, which is the 道 in 柔道 and 書道.

mnemonic: The doors open on a carriage that is already full, and the whole platform gets on regardless. No room in there, and up you go anyway: のる.
sentence_meaning: Please take a taxi from the station.
sentence: 駅からはタクシーに乗ってください。
notes: Takes に and not を: バスに乗る. 乗せる のせる is putting somebody else on board.

mnemonic: 牛 a cow walks in through 寺 the temple gate while the rest of the herd stands in the field. Out of forty of them they took Neil, only Neil: とくに.
sentence_meaning: I don't have any question in particular.
sentence: 特に質問はありません。
notes: Very often with a negative. 特に〜ない is not particularly.

sentence_meaning: This cookie is in the shape of a star.
mnemonic: 彡 three brush strokes on the right, doing the outlining. He cut a cheese into stars for the party and nobody ate a single one: かたち.
sentence: このクッキーは星の形です。
notes: 形 also reads けい in compounds, as in 形式 けいしき.

sentence_meaning: A: Which side do you think will win?B: Hmm... I don't know.
mnemonic: Asked which side will win, he lets the breath out slowly and looks at the ceiling. Nothing follows it. The whole answer is that noise: さあ.
sentence: A「どちらが勝つでしょうか。」B「さあ.....わかりません。」
notes: The same さあ gets things moving as well: さあ、行こう. Tone tells you which one you are hearing.
Same reading as 地 ち, ground. This is the one that comes out of you.
sentence: 血が出ていますよ。
mnemonic: 皿 a dish, and the mark above it is whatever got poured in. He raises his glass, says cheers, and only then sees what is running down your arm: ち.
sentence_meaning: You're bleeding.
He kept raising even more questions.
mnemonic: The questions got answered, came round again, then a third time on top of those. Sarah, knee going under the desk, stopped writing them down: さらに.
notes: 更 reads こう in compounds, as in 変更 へんこう. さらに piles more on top of what is already there.
sentence: 彼は更に質問を続けたの。

sentence_meaning: The meal is ready.
mnemonic: 用 a thing set out to be used, and 意 a sound sitting on a heart, your mind on it. The table was laid an hour early. Yo, we eat at seven: ようい.
sentence: 食事の用意ができました。
notes: 用意ができる is to be ready. 準備 じゅんび is the same idea a step more formal.

sentence_meaning: Yamada-san lost to Huang-san.
mnemonic: 貝 a shell for money with a figure stooped over it, carrying what he owes. Everyone else weighs in a salmon and you put down one mackerel: まける.
sentence: 山田さんはホアンさんに負けました。
notes: に marks whoever beat you: 山田さんに負けました. 勝つ かつ is to win.

mnemonic: 礻 an altar on the left with 申 speaking beside it, a man saying things to a wooden box in an empty field. Calm me, he keeps saying: かみ.
sentence_meaning: He believes in God.
notes: Three かみ in the deck and the kanji is what separates them: 神 god with 礻 an altar, 髪 hair with 髟 long hair, 紙 paper with 糸 thread.
sentence: 彼は神を信じている。

mnemonic: 宀 a roof with the crop safe under it, what a thing really turns out to be. Coats on, hand on the door, and he lands it like a jujitsu throw: じつは.
sentence_meaning: Actually, I'll be going back to my country next month.
sentence: 実は来月、帰国することになりました。
notes: Sets up news the listener did not have. 実 also reads み on its own, meaning fruit.

sentence: 昨日、服を買いました。
notes: 服を着る is to put them on. 履く はく is the verb for anything below the waist.
mnemonic: A hand laying cloth over a kneeling figure, fitted to the person inside it. She took a few into the booth, cool ones, and not one of them fit: ふく.
sentence_meaning: Yesterday, I bought clothes.

mnemonic: 不 cancels whatever comes after it, and 思議 is thinking a thing through and arguing it out. Neither got anywhere with the fish in ghee left on the doorstep: ふしぎ.
sentence_meaning: That's a very strange story.
sentence: それはとても不思議な話だね。
notes: It says the thing cannot be thought or argued out. Covers strange and wonderful both.

mnemonic: 識 sets 戈 a blade beside sound and speech, knowing a thing sharply. She is flat on the corridor floor and nobody can tell if anyone is home: is she keen? いしき.
sentence_meaning: He lost consciousness.
notes: 意識を失う is to lose consciousness. It also does awareness of a thing, as in 意識が高い.
sentence: 彼は意識を失いました。

notes: Goes in front of a question word to sharpen it: 一体何ですか, 一体誰が.
sentence: 一体何事ですか。
sentence_meaning: What on earth is going on?
mnemonic: 一 one and 体 a body, the whole thing balled up into a single question. You come home and he is sat at the table eating a tie: いったい.

sentence: とりあえずお知らせしておきます。
notes: Parks the decision rather than making it. とりあえずビール is the whole of Friday night in one word.
sentence_meaning: I will let them know for now.
mnemonic: The waiter is at the table and nobody has opened the menu. Beer, says Torrey. Ah, easy, and the rest gets sorted when it turns up: とりあえず.

sentence: 彼の家に荷物を送りました。
notes: Also seeing somebody off: 駅まで送る. 送別会 そうべつかい is the leaving do.
sentence_meaning: I sent a package to his house.
mnemonic: Two hands put the box down on 辶 the road and let go of it. Forty pounds at the counter to post a jumper: oh, cruel. おくる.

notes: じゃ is the spoken contraction of it. Same では as in 〜ではない, where it is doing a different job.
sentence: では、こちらはいかがですか。6万円です。
mnemonic: The first jacket is wrong and she has already turned to the rail behind her, saying nothing about it. Right then, this one? では.
sentence_meaning: Then how about this one? It's 60,000 yen.

sentence: それを聞いて安心しました。
notes: 安心する is to be relieved. 不安 ふあん is this same 安 with the 不 in front, so it is exactly this taken away.
mnemonic: 宀 a roof with 女 a woman settled under it, over 心 a heart. The test came back clear, her knees go, and she sits down hard on the step. Ann, your shin: あんしん.
sentence_meaning: I was relieved to hear that.
He lost his parents due to the earthquake.
mnemonic: 失 the hand that has let go without meaning to. The gate stood open all night and the field is empty this morning. Ooh, she is gone now: うしなう.
notes: Heavier than なくす. 失う takes what does not come back: a job, your sight, somebody. Same 失 as 失礼します.
sentence: 彼は地震で親を失いました。
彼の行動は理解できない。
notes: 行 reads こう in compounds, as in 銀行 ぎんこう. 行動する is to take action.
mnemonic: 行 the crossroads with 動 heavy things being shoved about by force. Not what he said he would do. What he actually did, on camera, at the co-op door: こうどう.
sentence_meaning: I can't understand his conduct.

sentence: 手と手が触れてどきどきしたよ。
notes: に marks what you touch: 手に触れる. It also does touching on a subject. 触る さわる is the deliberate hands-on one.
mnemonic: 角 a horn with 虫 an insect on it, a feeler going out to check what is there. Your hand meets hers on the handrail and there are suddenly very few rules: ふれる.
sentence_meaning: My heart pounded as our hands touched.
meaning: to touch, to come in contact with

sentence: 彼はそもそもこの仕事に向いていない。
notes: Reaches back past the argument to whether the thing should have started at all. Usually has a negative behind it.
mnemonic: The argument has been going an hour when somebody at the back points out the job was never his to take. Two sumo, and neither should be in the ring: そもそも.
sentence_meaning: He wasn't suited for this job in the first place.
There's not much rain this year.
mnemonic: Two inches of rain since April, a bicycle standing up out of the reservoir, and not enough left in it to scoop. Nigh on nothing: すくない.
notes: 少し すこし is a little, an amount. 少ない is the adjective, there are few of them.
sentence: 今年は雨が少ないです。

sentence_meaning: I wonder what he wanted to say after all.
mnemonic: 糸 the thread knotted off and 局 the office you end up in whatever else you tried. Three hours of arguing and the answer was on page one all along: けっきょく.
notes: 結果 けっか is the outcome itself. 結局 is the after all that comes in front of it.
sentence: 彼は結局何を言いたかったのだろう。
空が真っ青です。
notes: The same kanji is から empty in 空手 からて and くう in 空気 くうき. そら is the one over your head.
mnemonic: 穴 a hole with 工 a square under it, a space with nothing filling it. Flat on your back in the field, and the solar glare takes your eyebrows off: そら.
sentence_meaning: The sky is bright blue.

notes: Same reading as 住む すむ, to live somewhere. This one is a thing being over with. 〜ないで済む is getting away without having to.
sentence: 父の手術が無事に済みました。
mnemonic: 氵 water on the left, and you are up the far bank with the whole thing behind you. In at seven, out by nine, and somebody summed it up in three words: すむ.
sentence_meaning: My father's operation came off without a hitch.
I leave this work up to you.
mnemonic: The load is stacked up on the right and you have both hands in your pockets. The boat is his problem now. Mark, sell her if you like: まかせる.
meaning: to entrust to, to leave it to
sentence: この仕事は君に任せる。
notes: に marks who gets it: 君に任せる. 任せておいて is leave it with me.

sentence: 赤いコートを買いました。
notes: 赤ちゃん あかちゃん is a baby, red from the off. 赤 on its own is the colour.
mnemonic: A big figure stood over the fire, close enough to take its colour. Her coat coming up the street: a car, I said, and I was wrong by a mile. あかい.
sentence_meaning: I bought a red coat.

mnemonic: 大 big with 事 a matter being carried on, so a big matter. Not the ring and not the house. The one photograph. I would die, Jean. だいじ.
sentence_meaning: She is an important person to me.
sentence: 彼女は私の大事な人です。
notes: 大事にする is to treasure a thing. 大切 たいせつ is the near twin, and either does most of the time.

sentence: 彼女はメッセージを残しました。
notes: 残る のこる is a thing being left over. 残す is somebody leaving it deliberately.
mnemonic: 歹 the bare bones and blades again, except this time somebody left it there on purpose. Three words on the pad by the phone, no cost to her: のこす.
sentence_meaning: She left a message.

notes: 止める とめる is you stopping the thing. 止まる is it stopping, or sitting there stopped.
sentence: 道に大きいバスが止まっています。
meaning: to stop, to come to a stop
sentence_meaning: There is a big bus parked on the street.
mnemonic: 止 the flat footprint that goes nowhere else, and nobody parked this one. The bus has sat across the road since Tuesday. Tom, are you shifting it? とまる.

sentence_meaning: I wake up at 6 A.M. in the morning.
mnemonic: 日 the sun already up with 月 the moon not gone yet, both of them in the sky at once. Six in the morning, and somebody two doors down starts a saw: あさ.
notes: 今朝 けさ is this morning and does not use あさ at all. 朝ご飯 あさごはん is breakfast.
sentence: 朝、6時に起きます。
命より大切なものは無いよ。
notes: The life itself, not 生活 せいかつ which is how you live it. It reads めい in 命令 めいれい, an order.
sentence_meaning: There is nothing more important than life.
mnemonic: Handed down to the kneeling figure under the roof, and not a parcel. Up on the face it comes to one rope, one knot, and the man on the other end checking it twice: いのち.

sentence_meaning: I'm a bit worried since I have to go to the hospital for a check-up tomorrow.
mnemonic: 不 cancels whatever comes after it, and 安 is a woman settled under a roof. Take that away and you have the night before the hospital, awake at three: no fun. ふあん.
notes: The 安 of 安心 あんしん with 不 in front of it, so it is precisely that peace of mind removed.
sentence: 明日、病院に検査に行くので少し不安です。

mnemonic: 糸 a thread tied off and 構 the frame already built. Nothing more is going in. Your hand goes flat over the glass before the bottle is halfway across: けっこう.
sentence_meaning: I am full so no seconds for me, thank you.
sentence: お腹がいっぱいなのでお代わりは結構です。
notes: Same word as 結構 "quite". This one turns things down, politely and firmly, and the tone is what tells you which you are getting.

sentence_meaning: Glasses suit her quite well.
mnemonic: The very same word said the very same way, doing a different job. Nobody expected the glasses to suit her and they suit her more than a bit: けっこう.
notes: Same word as 結構 "all right, no thank you". This one goes in front of an adjective: 結構高い, quite expensive.
sentence: 彼女は結構めがねが似合うね。

mnemonic: 立 standing, 木 a tree, 斤 an axe already in it, timber cut this morning. He got the car at a rally, she says, and he has told every single person: あたらしい.
sentence_meaning: His car is new.
sentence: 彼の車は新しい。
notes: 新しい is the adjective. 新 reads しん in compounds, as in 新聞 しんぶん.

sentence_meaning: If it's an injury of such a small extent then it'll be fine.
mnemonic: 禾 grain, because this began as weighing out a crop to see how much of it there was. How bad is the cut? A graze. Nurses see worse: they do, daily. ていど.
notes: How far along a scale a thing sits. この程度 is this much, and 〜程度 after a number is about that many.
sentence: この程度の怪我なら大丈夫です。

notes: Also the wall you hit: 壁にぶつかる is to come up against a problem.
sentence: 壁に絵が掛かっている。
mnemonic: 土 earth down at the bottom, because you built this out of the field it stands in. He misjudged the car bay by six inches and the garage has a new window: かべ.
sentence_meaning: There's a painting on the wall.

sentence: 私に何か用ですか。
notes: 何か用ですか is do you need something. As a suffix it is made for: 子供用 for children. Same 用 as 用意 ようい.
sentence_meaning: Do you need me for something?
mnemonic: Somebody has been stood in your doorway for a while now saying nothing at all, so in the end you have to be the one to ask. Yo. What is it you actually want? よう.
meaning: things to do, (as a suffix) to do..., made for...

notes: 背 on its own also does height: 背が高い is tall.
sentence: 背中がかゆいです。
mnemonic: Two figures back to back, and 中 the dead centre of them. The one patch you cannot reach has itched since Tuesday. Senna? A car key? Anything: せなか.
sentence_meaning: My back itches.
I cut my hair, but my husband didn't even notice.
mnemonic: 気 steam off a person and 付 a hand pressing something on until it sticks. Four inches came off her hair and by nine he has only asked where his keys are: きづく.
notes: に marks what you notice: 間違いに気付く. Same 付 as 付ける つける.
sentence: 私が髪を切ったのに、夫は気付きませんでした。

meaning: all of a sudden, without warning
sentence_meaning: Someone suddenly tapped on my shoulder from behind.
mnemonic: A hand lands flat on your shoulder from behind and nobody made a sound getting there. Eek, and in a hurry, really: いきなり.
notes: The abrupt spoken one. 突然 とつぜん is the written version and 急に きゅうに is a state changing fast.
sentence: 後ろからいきなり肩を叩かれた。

sentence_meaning: I handed him the letter.
mnemonic: 氵 water, because this began as getting a thing over a river. She has been talking for an hour, so you put the glass into her hand: water, Sue. わたす.
meaning: to carry across, to hand over
sentence: 彼に手紙を渡しました。
notes: に marks who gets it: 彼に渡す. 渡る わたる is you crossing over yourself.

meaning: to be happy, to be delighted
mnemonic: The drum and the mouth beneath it are making the same racket, and both meant to. She got the news at four and by six your local pub knows: よろこぶ.
sentence_meaning: She was very pleased.
notes: Used about other people being pleased. 嬉しい うれしい is how you say it about yourself.
sentence: 彼女はとても喜びました。

notes: Written in kana as often as not. かわいそう looks related but means poor thing, not cute.
sentence: 妹は可愛い服が大好きです。
mnemonic: 可 the yes you are permitted to give, and 愛 a heart carried about in the middle of it. The puppy has one ear inside out and is giving you the full cow eye: かわいい.
sentence_meaning: My younger sister loves cute clothes.

mnemonic: 女 at 台 the platform again, except this time nobody pushed. The new job started at nine whether your coat was off or not. Ha, Jim, are you ready? はじまる.
sentence_meaning: My new job started.
sentence: 新しい仕事が始まりました。
notes: 始める はじめる is you starting it. 始まる is it starting, ready or not.

sentence: すてきな色のセーターですね。
notes: 色々 いろいろ is various, colours upon colours. 色 also reads しょく in compounds.
mnemonic: Nobody agrees what the two figures in this one are doing, so take the meaning and go. That jumper is a shade with no name and it has started a row: いろ.
sentence_meaning: That sweater is a wonderful color.

sentence: 父が彼女との結婚を認めてくれました。
notes: Does recognising a fact, admitting it, and giving permission, all with one word. 間違いを認める is to admit a mistake.
sentence_meaning: My father accepted my marriage to her.
mnemonic: 言 speech with 忍 endure under it, words held in until they have to come out. Her father set his glass down and said yes to the marriage: meet Tom, our lad. みとめる.
meaning: to recognize, to approve, to accept

sentence: 午後急に空が暗くなりました。
notes: Same reading as 九 きゅう, nine. 急に きゅうに is the adverb and 急ぐ いそぐ is to hurry.
sentence_meaning: The sky suddenly got dark in the afternoon.
mnemonic: A hand snatching down at a heart, which is what the chest does. Four in the afternoon and the sky shuts like a lid while you cross the yard: きゅう.
向 the window that faces one way out, and this is whatever is at the other end of the look. Your friend is across the field, past the one moo cow: むこう.
sentence_meaning: My friend is over there.
meaning: the other side, the other party, opponent
sentence: 友達は向こうにいます。
notes: Also the other party in a deal or a fight. 向かう むかう heads that way, 向ける むける aims something, 向こう is the far end.

sentence_meaning: Children need their parents' love.
mnemonic: 求 a fur coat with the tails still on it and everybody in the village wanting it. She is not after the toy. What she is after costs nothing and is more to me: もとめる.
notes: More formal than ほしい. It does seeking, requesting and demanding: 助けを求める is to call for help.
sentence: 子供は親の愛を求めます。

sentence_meaning: My shoulder hurts.
mnemonic: 戸 a door hung on 月 the flesh, which is what this is: a hinge that takes the weight. You carried the bag on it all day and now it will not lift: かた.
sentence: 肩が痛いです。
notes: Same reading as 方 かた, the polite word for a person, and later 型 かた, a type or mould. 肩が凝る is stiff shoulders.

mnemonic: 亻 a person right in 中 the middle of the group, with 間 the gap between them closed up. Nobody signed anything, they just kept turning up. Na, come on: なかま.
sentence_meaning: He has a lot of comrades.
sentence: 彼には仲間がたくさんいる。
notes: Warmer than 友達 ともだち, and it works for a crew or a band. 仲がいい なかがいい is to get on well.
The relief kind of at last. やっと is its close twin and does the same job in speech.
sentence: ようやくゴールが見えてきました。
mnemonic: Six hours up the pass and the tent is finally in sight, with the yak that beat you there already sat down. Yo, yak, you: ようやく.
sentence_meaning: At last, we could see the goal.
I was so happy I started crying without realizing it.
mnemonic: 田 a field on 心 a heart, and this time the heart got there first. The news landed and you were crying before any of it reached your head: oh, Moe was too. おもわず.
notes: A thing happening before you decided to do it. 思う おもう with the thinking taken out of it.
sentence: 嬉しくて思わず涙が出ました。

notes: With a negative it is hardly any, with a positive almost all. ほとんどない and ほとんど全部 both work.
sentence: お金がほとんどありません。
sentence_meaning: I have hardly any money.
mnemonic: The tin is out, the oven is hot, and there is not enough flour left in the bag to call it anything. Hot oven, no dough: ほとんど.

sentence: 彼は突然走り出したのよ。
notes: The written and formal one. いきなり is the abrupt spoken version, 急に きゅうに is a state changing fast. Shares its 然 with 全然 and 当然.
sentence_meaning: He suddenly began to run.
mnemonic: 穴 a hole with 犬 a dog bursting straight out of it, and 然 that being how things are. He was walking beside you, then he was forty yards up the road: とつぜん.
自 the nose you point at to mean me, with 身 a whole body drawn out in profile. Not your name and not your job. The one actually stood there: じしん.
sentence_meaning: Don't doubt yourself.
sentence: 自分自身を疑ってはいけません。
notes: 自分自身 じぶんじしん doubles it for emphasis. Later comes 自信 じしん, self-confidence, which sounds identical and is written with 信.

mnemonic: You put the cat out at eleven, and at midnight there is a foot, a tabby, and the whole business to go through again: ふたたび.
sentence_meaning: He came back here once again.
sentence: 彼は再びここに戻ってきた。
notes: Written and a shade formal. また is the everyday again. 再 reads さい in compounds: 再会 さいかい.

mnemonic: 青 fresh and still down the left side. Out at the end of the lane the loudest thing all afternoon is a car three fields off: she is a car, then nothing. しずか.
sentence_meaning: I like quiet places.
notes: 静かに しずかに is quietly. 静か takes な in front of a noun.
sentence: 静かな所が好きです。

notes: Also jumping: 飛び込む とびこむ is to leap in. 跳ぶ is the spelling for jumping specifically.
sentence: 鳥が飛んでいます。
sentence_meaning: A bird is flying.
mnemonic: It came off the fence post with no run-up at all and was over the hedge before you had the camera up. To boot, it took the sandwich: とぶ.

notes: Also blank: 白紙 はくし is a blank sheet. 白 reads はく as well as しろ.
sentence: 彼は歯が白い。
sentence_meaning: His teeth are white.
mnemonic: 白 the sun just clearing the horizon, the whitest thing going. He smiles and the pub goes quiet, and she, Roy, the lot of them, just stare: しろい.

sentence: 昨日、父から手紙が届いた。
notes: The thing arriving, not you sending it. 届ける とどける is you delivering it. 手が届く is to be able to reach something.
sentence_meaning: I received a letter from my father yesterday.
mnemonic: 尸 a shelter with 由 a channel running into it. The parcel arrives while you are out and sits on the step waiting for your toe to dock into: とどく.

sentence_meaning: Our cat had kittens.
mnemonic: 生 the same shoot forcing its way up. The cat went under the shed on Tuesday and came out with four on Thursday, and all anyone heard was a low hum: うむ.
sentence: うちのネコが子猫を生みました。
notes: 生む is bearing offspring, and 産む is the more usual spelling for giving birth. 生まれる うまれる is being born.

mnemonic: 亻 a person and 到 arriving, except on the floor. He clips the gate and the pole goes flat behind him. Ta, and he owes the course a new one: たおす.
sentence_meaning: That skier knocked the pole down.
notes: 倒れる たおれる is it going over by itself. 倒す is you putting it down.
sentence: そのスキーヤーはポールを倒した。

meaning: to look similar to, to resemble
mnemonic: 亻 a person with 以 beside them, one thing held up against another. Same jaw, same walk, same way of standing in a doorway. Nearer than you would like: にる.
sentence_meaning: I look like my mother and my older sister looks like my father.
notes: に marks who you take after: 母に似ている. It nearly always turns up in the ている form.
sentence: 私は母に、姉は父に似ています。

mnemonic: 穴 an empty space with 気 the steam that rises through it anyway. Out past the last farm you take a lungful and it is better than the cookie you brought with you: くうき.
sentence_meaning: The air is very clear in the countryside.
sentence: 田舎は空気がとても美味しいです。
notes: Also the air in a room in the social sense: 空気を読む くうきをよむ is reading the mood.

mnemonic: 月 the flesh sense with 要 next to it, hands on a waist from way back. Bend down once for a dropped sock and it goes like somebody took a cosh to you: こし.
sentence_meaning: I've had a pain in my lower back since yesterday.
sentence: 昨日から腰が痛い。
notes: The whole lower back and hips, not just the hip joint. 腰が痛い is the everyday complaint.

mnemonic: 夕 an evening with 口 a mouth under it. Not the whole 名前, just the part of it people go on repeating after you have left the room: な.
sentence_meaning: What is your name?
notes: 名前 なまえ is the everyday word for a name. 名 on its own leans towards reputation, and 有名 ゆうめい is famous.
sentence: 君の名は何？

sentence_meaning: There are many cars on this road so it's dangerous.
mnemonic: 危 a figure at a cliff edge and 険 the steep mound beside it, both ground you come off. Cars both ways, no pavement, somebody yelling keep in, Ken: きけん.
notes: 危険 works as a noun and with な in front of a noun. 危ない あぶない is the spoken one you shout.
sentence: この道は車が多くて、危険です。

mnemonic: 亻 a person and 寸 a hand, the same press as 付ける except nobody pressed. You crossed the yard and the mud came with you. Took the whole walk home to notice: つく.
sentence_meaning: I have mud on my shoes.
meaning: to attach itself to, to be connected with, to come in contact with
sentence: 靴に泥が付いています。
notes: 付ける つける is you attaching it, 付く is it attaching itself. Three つく to keep apart: this one, つく for a light coming on, and 着く for arriving.

sentence: 部屋の電気がついています。
notes: Also written 点く. 点ける つける is somebody switching it on; this is it being on. Same reading as 付く つく, which is about sticking to things.
sentence_meaning: The room light is on.
mnemonic: Written in kana here, but it is the 点 of 点ける with nobody near the switch. You come back from the shops and the front room is already glowing at you: つく.
meaning: to be on, to be switched on

sentence: このスープはとても熱い。
notes: 熱い is hot to the touch. 暑い あつい is hot weather, same reading and a different kanji. 熱 ねつ on its own is a fever.
mnemonic: 灬 four dots of fire underneath, and the bowl above them has had an hour of it. The soup goes in and comes straight back out again, and the spoon goes down: あつい.
sentence_meaning: This soup is very hot.

notes: The set reply is おかえり, or おかえりなさい. Used coming back to the office as well as the house.
sentence: ただいま。
mnemonic: The door goes, the bag hits the floor, and a man who has been no further than the shops announces himself like a stage act. Ta-da, I am home: ただいま.
sentence_meaning: I'm back!
Thank you for the meal.
mnemonic: 頂 the same crown of the head as 頂く, and down it goes again. Hands together over the bowl, and not one grain moves until it has been said: いただきます.
meaning: let's eat!, thank you for the meal
sentence: 頂きます。
notes: The humble "I receive", said before eating. ごちそうさま is its pair afterwards. Same 頂 as 頂く いただく.

sentence: そんなに慌ててどこに行くの。
notes: 慌てないで is do not panic. It is the flapping about, not the fear underneath it.
mnemonic: 忄 a heart with everything running wild alongside it. He is halfway out of the door with one shoe on and the kettle still going: ah, water, all over the floor. あわてる.
sentence_meaning: Where are you going in such a hurry?
If you speak loudly it will be a bother to people around you.
mnemonic: 周 the whole way round, and 囲 a 囗 border closed on 井 a well. Everyone inside earshot, which at that volume is the entire room: しゅうい.
sentence: 大声で話すと周囲の人に迷惑ですよ。
notes: The people and things around you. 周り まわり is the everyday word for the same idea.

sentence: 早起きした日は気分がいいです。
notes: 気分がいい is feeling good. 気持ち きもち is nearer a physical sensation; 気分 is the mood you are in.
mnemonic: 気 the steam off a person with 分 a portion cut from it, so this is your share of it today. Up at six, a key still in the door, and a warm bun on the side: きぶん.
sentence_meaning: On days I wake up early, I feel good.

notes: Same 実 as 実は じつは. 事実 is the fact itself; 真実 しんじつ is the truth of the matter.
sentence: それは全て事実ですか。
mnemonic: 事 a matter being carried on and 実 the crop safe under its roof. Not the version anybody wanted, and not the one in the report either. The one that happened: じじつ.
sentence_meaning: Is that all true?

mnemonic: The machine will not say a word to you until the card is in. Not the amount, not the receipt, that first. Every maze starts at the one entrance: まず.
sentence_meaning: First, please insert your cash card.
sentence: まずキャッシュカードを入れてください。
notes: Sets up the first step of a sequence. とりあえず is doing something provisionally rather than first.

sentence_meaning: No, I'm serious.
mnemonic: 本 the root a thing grows from with 気 the steam rising off a person, so what is actually down there underneath all of it. He is not joking this time: ほんき.
notes: 本気で is seriously, and 本気? on its own is are you serious.
sentence: いや、僕は本気なんだ。

mnemonic: She never actually said yes. The chin went down once, 頁 the head doing the entire job, and nobody in the room needed anything more than that: うなずく.
sentence_meaning: She showed agreement with a nod.
notes: The nod itself. 賛成する さんせいする is agreeing out loud.
sentence: 彼女は頷いて同意を示したの。

notes: 通り is the street. Hung on the end of a word it means as per: 予定通り よていどおり, on schedule.
sentence: ここが町で一番広い通りです。
sentence_meaning: This is the widest street in the city.
mnemonic: 辶 the road radical, and this one carries on rather than stopping. Widest in town, and you could tour it end to end inside ten minutes: とおり.

notes: 想像する is to imagine. 想像力 そうぞうりょく is imagination as a faculty.
sentence: そんなことは想像できないよ。
sentence_meaning: I can't imagine such a thing.
mnemonic: 想 what forms over 心 a heart when the thing is not there, and 像 a person stood next to 象 an elephant. There is no elephant. A whole zoo of nothing: そうぞう.

sentence: 私はこの店によく来ます。
notes: Same みせ as 見せる みせる, to show, which is where the word comes from. お店 おみせ is the polite form.
mnemonic: 广 a shelter with a claim staked under it, and the place where things are 見せる shown to you. Same man behind the counter, starting your order before you speak: みせ.
sentence_meaning: I come to this store quite often.

notes: 何 reads なん here. It marks a feeling you cannot account for.
sentence: 茶柱が立って、何だか少し幸せな気分です。
mnemonic: 何 the same what-on-earth as なに. The tea leaf stands upright in the cup and the whole morning improves, and you could not tell anybody why: なんだか.
sentence_meaning: Seeing the tea leaves floating upright, somehow I feel happy.

notes: 目的 is the aim itself. 目標 もくひょう is the target you set in order to reach it.
sentence: 彼が来た目的が分かりません。
sentence_meaning: I don't understand the purpose of his visit.
mnemonic: 目 an eye and 的 the white circle you aim it at. Not why he came, which nobody knows, but the thing he was aiming for: もくてき.

sentence: 昨日は8時間眠りました。
notes: 寝る ねる is lying down to sleep. 眠る is being asleep. 眠い ねむい is sleepy.
mnemonic: 目 an eye with the lids down, and that is all there is to it. Not getting into bed, which is 寝る, but the eight hours you were not present for: ねむる.
sentence_meaning: I slept for eight hours yesterday.

meaning: certainly, surely, if I'm not mistaken...
sentence_meaning: If I'm not mistaken, the meeting tomorrow starts at 3:00.
mnemonic: 石 a stone, solid enough to lean on, except this one wobbles a bit. The meeting is at three. Ta, she can check it if you want it in writing: たしか.
notes: 確かに means definitely. 確か in front of a statement does the opposite, hedging it: fairly sure, would not swear to it.
sentence: 明日の会議は確か３時からだと思います。
お金はまだ十分あります。
notes: Also written 充分. Careful: 十分 also reads じっぷん, meaning ten minutes, with the same two characters.
mnemonic: 十 ten and 分 the parts, so all ten tenths of it. Money still in the account at month end, and enough left to chew a bun on the way home: じゅうぶん.
sentence_meaning: We still have plenty of money.

mnemonic: 米 rice measured out on the left, and 理 the sense a thing makes on the right. Ingredients weighed, then put in an order that works. That is the whole of it: りょうり.
sentence_meaning: This is Japanese cooking.
sentence: これは日本の料理です。
notes: 料理する is to cook. 日本料理 is Japanese cuisine and 料理人 りょうりにん is a cook.

sentence: 子供の頃、よくその公園で遊んだ。
notes: 子供の頃 is when I was a child. After a word it softens to ごろ: 三時頃 さんじごろ, around three.
mnemonic: Not the date, and nobody is asking for the date. The stretch of years when you were small enough to be in that park every single day: ころ.
sentence_meaning: I often played in that park when I was a kid.

sentence: 彼女は絵がなかなか上手です。
notes: With a positive it is better than expected. With a negative it is not easily: なかなか来ない, he is taking forever.
sentence_meaning: She's pretty good at painting.
mnemonic: You expected the painting to be alright. It is not alright, it is good, and you have said so twice before you have decided to: なかなか.

sentence: 彼女はとても正直だ。
notes: 正直に言うと is to be honest. It works as a character trait and as the adverb.
mnemonic: 正 pulling up exactly on the mark and 直 an eye looking dead ahead. Neither of them goes round anything. She gives you the answer you were hoping to avoid: しょうじき.
sentence_meaning: She's very honest.

mnemonic: Not your name, not your things. The one item you cannot put down, leave in the hotel safe, or ask somebody to mind: み.
sentence_meaning: Personal safety is paramount while traveling.
notes: 身 is you as a physical person. 体 からだ is the body as an object. 身分 みぶん is your standing.
sentence: 旅行中は身の安全が第一です。

sentence_meaning: I am full.
mnemonic: Two helpings in and somebody comes round with a third. Your hand goes flat over the plate before you have thought about it. Not one more pie: いっぱい.
notes: お腹がいっぱい is full up. In front of a noun it means a lot of: 人がいっぱい.
sentence: お腹がいっぱいです。
この絵は美しいです。
notes: More written and more formal than きれい. きれい also covers clean and tidy; this one does not.
mnemonic: 羊 a sheep drawn 大 big, which was somebody's old idea of a fine thing. You stop dead in front of the picture and hold up everyone behind you: うつくしい.
sentence_meaning: This picture is beautiful.

mnemonic: One forkful and the table goes quiet, because it is not sweet, it is far too sweet, and nobody wants to be the one to say so. Ah, my: あまい.
sentence_meaning: This cake is sweet, isn't it?
sentence: このケーキは甘いですね。
notes: Also indulgent and soft on people: 甘い親 is a lenient parent, and 甘える あまえる is trading on it.

mnemonic: Call him an architect and you get corrected before the sentence has landed. Not an architect. An artist. He is the one who put mushrooms in the risotto: むしろ.
sentence_meaning: He's an artist rather than an architect.
sentence: 彼は建築家というよりむしろ芸術家ね。
notes: Corrects a comparison: not A, or rather B. Usually with より or というより in front of it.

sentence: きりんの首は長い。
notes: 首になる くびになる is to be fired, the same idea as getting the chop.
sentence_meaning: The neck of giraffes are long.
mnemonic: On a giraffe there is an absurd amount of it. You follow it up, and up, and run out of sky before you get to the head: くび.
咸 all of it landing on 心 a heart, and 情 a second heart tucked under 青. Two hearts in one word, which is about right for the subject. Can Joe explain any of it? かんじょう.
sentence_meaning: Emotions are complex things.
sentence: 感情とは複雑なものです。
notes: The emotion itself. 感じ かんじ is the impression you get; 気持ち きもち is nearer a physical sensation.

sentence_meaning: There are cherry blossoms around the house.
mnemonic: 周 a border drawn the whole way round. Cherry trees on every side of the house, so whichever window you open the view is the same one: まわり.
sentence: 家の周りに桜の木があります。
notes: The everyday word. 周囲 しゅうい is the same idea in writing.

sentence_meaning: Please teach me a way to get good at Japanese.
mnemonic: 方 which way a thing faces, and 法 water finding the one route down. Not what to do. The road by which it gets done, and you would like it written out: ほうほう.
notes: 方法 is the method. やり方 やりかた is the more spoken way of doing it.
sentence: 日本語が上手になる方法を教えてください。
もう一度言います。
notes: Built from もう and 一度 いちど, both already in the deck. もう一回 もういっかい does the same job.
sentence_meaning: I will say it one more time.
mnemonic: もう pointed forwards again, with 一度 the single turn of the wheel. He said it once, nobody moved, so here it comes with exactly the same patience: もういちど.

sentence: 前の車はとても遅い。
notes: Does slow and late both, so it is the opposite of 早い はやい and of 速い はやい at once.
mnemonic: 辶 a road with something on it that is in no rush at all. The car in front has done forty for six miles and there is nowhere to pass: oh, so slow. おそい.
sentence_meaning: The car in front is very slow.

sentence: 親子の会話は大切です。
notes: Same 話 as 話す はなす. 会話 is the exchange itself rather than the talking.
mnemonic: 会 people gathering in under a roof, and 話 a tongue doing the work. Not one person talking. The part where it goes back and forth, which is the part that counts: かいわ.
sentence_meaning: Conversation between parents and children is important.

mnemonic: 𠆢 a lid coming down onto 口 a mouth, the two halves meeting exactly. New shoes on, and you walk the length of the shop without thinking about your feet once: あう.
sentence_meaning: These shoes fit me.
sentence: この靴は私の足に合っている。
notes: Same reading as 会う あう, to meet. This one is things matching: shoes fitting, sums agreeing, 話が合う getting on with somebody. 合わせる あわせる is you making them match.

sentence: フランスからサーカスがやって来ます。
notes: More vivid than 来る on its own. It carries the sense of having come all that way to get here.
sentence_meaning: A circus is coming from France.
mnemonic: やる doing and 来る coming, bolted together. Not simply arriving. Making the entire journey and turning up on the doorstep, big top and all, from France: やってくる.
meaning: to come around, to come along

mnemonic: Three 木 trees, and then a great many more. Twenty minutes in, the light has changed and you cannot hear the road any more: もり.
sentence_meaning: I like to walk in the forest.
notes: 森 is the forest and 林 はやし is the wood. 森林 しんりん puts them together for woodland in general.
sentence: 私は森を歩くのが好きです。
みんなで大きいテーブルを動かします。
notes: 動く うごく is it moving. 動かす is you moving it.
sentence_meaning: Everyone moves the big table together.
mnemonic: 重 something heavy with 力 power behind it, the same as 動く, except this time it is you doing the shoving. Six of you round one table: oo, go on, cuss if it helps. うごかす.
meaning: to move, to make a move

notes: 能力がある is capable. 力 ちから on its own is strength; 能力 is capability.
sentence: 彼は能力のある社員です。
mnemonic: 能 whatever a thing turns out to be able to do, with 力 an arm bent hard at the elbow next to it. Not what he was hired for. What he can actually do: のうりょく.
sentence_meaning: He's a capable employee.

sentence: 彼は寒くて震えていました。
notes: 地震 じしん is an earthquake, the same 震. 震える is a person shaking rather than the ground.
mnemonic: 雨 up top, and whatever sits under it will not keep still. He came in from the yard blue round the mouth and could not get the cup to his face: flu, or just cold. ふるえる.
sentence_meaning: He was cold and shivering.

notes: 期待する is to expect in the hopeful sense. 予想 よそう is a flat prediction with no hope in it.
sentence: みんな私たちに期待しています。
sentence_meaning: Everyone has expectations of us.
mnemonic: 月 counting off the months, and 待 somebody stood outside the temple waiting. Everyone has decided in advance how this goes. Key in one hand, tie straightened: きたい.

sentence: 無事、家に着きました。
notes: 無事に is safely. It means nothing went wrong, not that nothing happened.
mnemonic: 無 everything burnt away to nothing and 事 a matter to deal with. No matters at all, which is the point. Home, and the budgie is still alive: ぶじ.
sentence_meaning: I arrived home safely.

mnemonic: 走 running with 己 yourself behind it, the same standing-up as 起きる, except somebody made it happen. He threw the first punch and the whole street had a night of it: おこす.
sentence_meaning: He caused a violent incident.
sentence: 彼は暴力事件を起こしたんだよ。
notes: Same word as 起こす "to wake up". 起きる おきる is a thing happening by itself; 起こす is somebody causing it.
Same word as 起こす "to cause". 起きる おきる is getting up yourself; 起こす is getting somebody else up.
sentence: 明日、6時に起こしてください。
sentence_meaning: Please wake me up tomorrow at six o'clock.
mnemonic: The very same 起こす. What you are standing upright this time is a person, at six in the morning, against their considerable preference: おこす.

notes: 耳がいい is good hearing. 聞く きく is the listening you do with it.
sentence: 彼女は耳がよく聞こえません。
mnemonic: A pictograph drawn side on, and you have two of them. Say something across the room and she turns the good one towards you: me? me? みみ.
sentence_meaning: Her hearing isn't very good.
My friend had a baby.
mnemonic: 生 the shoot pushing its way up, except this time nobody is doing it to anybody. The phone goes at four in the morning and there is a new person in the world: うまれる.
sentence: 友達に子供が生まれました。
notes: 生む うむ is bearing the child; 生まれる is the child arriving. 生まれ うまれ on its own is where you are from.

sentence: 私たちはレンタカーで移動しました。
notes: 移動する is moving from place to place. 引っ越す ひっこす is moving house.
sentence_meaning: We traveled around by a rental car.
mnemonic: 禾 grain being shifted about in 多 quantity, and 動 heavy things moved by force. Not a stroll. Getting an entire party and its luggage from one place to the next: いどう.

sentence_meaning: This big luggage is a big hindrance.
mnemonic: 牙 a fang, 阝 a mound, and 魔 the demon out of 魔法 alongside. The suitcase is in the hall and everybody has to go round it. A jam, and somebody's fault: じゃま.
sentence: この大きい荷物はとても邪魔です。
notes: 邪魔する is to get in the way. お邪魔します is said entering somebody's home, apologising for being the obstacle.

sentence_meaning: The children are playing in the park.
mnemonic: 辶 a road with no destination attached to it. Nobody has told them what the game is and nobody needs to. Two hours in the park and not one plan between them: あそぶ.
notes: Covers playing and going out to enjoy yourself. 遊びに行く is going round to somebody's, not necessarily to play.
sentence: 子供たちが公園で遊んでいる。

mnemonic: 要 the part everything else hangs off, out of 必要. Walk in off the street with no booking and they seat you anyway. Whatever it was, it was not needed: いる.
sentence_meaning: Reservations are not required.
sentence: 予約は要りません。
notes: Same reading as いる, to exist, and usually written in kana, so context does the work. It takes が: お金が要る.

sentence: もうお金が無くなりました。
notes: Used up or gone missing, both. Careful with 亡くなる なくなる, identical in speech, which is the polite word for somebody dying.
sentence_meaning: I've run out of money already.
mnemonic: 無 the whole lot burnt away to nothing, with なる the turning into. It was there this morning. Where it went has stopped being the interesting question: なくなる.
meaning: to be lost, to be used up

notes: 口 くち is the mouth and 唇 くちびる begins with it. リップ is the loanword on the cosmetics.
sentence: 彼女の唇はとても可愛いです。
mnemonic: 口 a mouth down at the bottom, which is why the word opens with くち. The visible edge of it, and hers are the part everybody comments on: くちびる.
sentence_meaning: Her lips are really cute.
I'm wearing a suit today.
mnemonic: 着 the same character as arriving, because this is clothes arriving on you. Suit on at seven for a nine o'clock meeting, and it stays on until midnight: きる.
notes: Worn on the upper or whole body. 履く はく is anything below the waist. Same reading as 切る きる, to cut, which the kanji keeps apart.
sentence: 今日はスーツを着ています。

mnemonic: 色 a colour, and 々 saying do that one again, so colours upon colours. He knows a bit about everything and intends to cover all of it: いろいろ.
sentence_meaning: He knows about a lot of things.
notes: 々 means repeat the character before it, so this is 色色. It comes back six more times in this deck, in 人々, 我々, 日々, 少々, 元々 and 様々.
sentence: 彼は色々なことを知っている。

sentence_meaning: This way please.
mnemonic: He holds the door open with his back and waits. Nothing is said and nothing needs saying, because the whole invitation is in the eyebrows: どうぞ.
notes: Offers and invites: take it, go ahead, after you. どうも is thanks, and the two get muddled constantly.
sentence: こちらへどうぞ。

notes: Both halves are words you already have. It is also what a computer does when it boots.
sentence: 彼は急に立ち上がったの。
mnemonic: 立つ standing and 上がる going up, welded together. He was sat down a second ago, the chair has scraped, and the whole table has stopped talking: たちあがる.
sentence_meaning: He suddenly stood up.

sentence: 必死の思いで彼に頼んだよ。
notes: The thought or feeling itself, from 思う おもう. Later comes 重い おもい, heavy, which sounds identical.
sentence_meaning: I asked him out of desperation.
mnemonic: 田 a field sat on 心 a heart, and this is what stays up there rather than what you do about it. He asked her, and asking cost him everything he had: おもい.

notes: Same 以 as 以上 and 以外. 以前 is before some point; 前 まえ on its own is simply ago.
sentence: 以前彼はこの町に住んでいたんだ。
mnemonic: 以 the marker that fixes a boundary, and 前 everything in front of it. He lived here once, on the far side of that line, and the shop still remembers him: いぜん.
sentence_meaning: He used to live in this town.

sentence: もう少しゆっくり話してください。
notes: Both halves are already in the deck. もうちょっと is the casual version of the same request.
sentence_meaning: Please speak a little slower.
mnemonic: もう pointed forwards, and 少し the scooch left in the glass. Not slower. A bit slower, and he is asking nicely because he stopped following two sentences ago: もうすこし.
meaning: a little more, a bit more

sentence_meaning: Some climbers were attacked by a bear in the mountains.
mnemonic: A dragon with 衣 clothing under it, arriving from above and giving nobody a say. The climbers heard nothing until it was already between them and the tents: おそう.
sentence: 山で登山客が熊に襲われたよ。
notes: Used of animals, weather and crime. 攻撃 こうげき is a deliberate assault, and more military.

meaning: to be found, to be caught
sentence_meaning: I can't find my glasses.
mnemonic: 見 an eye and 付 a hand fixing onto what it saw, the same as 見つける, except nobody is looking. The glasses turn up or they do not, and today they do not: みつかる.
notes: 見つける みつける is you finding it. 見つかる is it being found, or you being caught.
sentence: メガネが見つかりません。
時間がないので、急いでください。
notes: Same 急 as 急 きゅう, sudden. 急いで いそいで is quickly, said as an instruction.
mnemonic: A hand snatching down at a heart, the same 急 you have as きゅう. Fifteen minutes to cross town, and he is putting his coat on inside the lift: いそぐ.
sentence_meaning: We don't have much time, so please hurry.

sentence: せっかく来たんだからゆっくりして行きなさい。
notes: Marks effort already made that would otherwise go to waste. せっかくだから is since we are here anyway.
mnemonic: Two trains and a bus to get here, and now you are talking about leaving. Sit down. The effort is spent either way, so spend the afternoon too: せっかく.
sentence_meaning: Since you've come all the way, why don't you stay for a while?

notes: Same reading as 下りる おりる. 降りる is getting off or out of something: a bus, a train, a car.
