sentence: ここでバスを降ります。
meaning: to get off, to go down
sentence_meaning: I'm getting off the bus here.
mnemonic: 阝 a mound, and somebody picking their way down off it. The bus is still moving and you are already at the door with a hand on the rail: おりる.
The same おりる, written with 下, the mark that sits below the line. Not off anything. Simply down, one stair at a time, at the end of the corridor: おりる.
sentence_meaning: Please go down those stairs.
meaning: to go down, to come down
sentence: そこの階段を下りてください。
notes: Same reading as 降りる おりる. 下りる is going down stairs or a hill; 降りる is getting off a vehicle.

sentence: この紙を半分に切ってください。
notes: Same reading as 着る きる, to wear. Also switching off and cutting off: 電話を切る is hanging up.
sentence_meaning: Please cut this paper in half.
mnemonic: 刀 a blade on the right, and everything to its left is what the blade meets. Fold the paper, run a thumb down the crease, then take the scissors to it: きる.
事 a matter being carried on, with 件 counting them off one at a time. Not a thing that happened. A thing that happened and now has a file with a number on it: じけん.
sentence_meaning: The perpetrator of that incident hasn't been caught yet.
sentence: その事件の犯人はまだ捕まっていない。
notes: An incident serious enough to be reported on. 事故 じこ is an accident.

sentence: 友達からメールの返事が中々来ません。
notes: Same 返 as 返す かえす. 返事する is to reply, and 返事がない is the silence you get instead.
mnemonic: 返 something turned round and sent back down the road, and 事 the matter itself. You sent it on Tuesday and there is still nothing in the box: へんじ.
sentence_meaning: My friend won't respond to my mail.

mnemonic: 酉 a wine jar, and everything too strong that ever came out of one. The review does not say the food was poor. It names the chef: ひどい.
sentence_meaning: I got a terrible score on yesterday's test.
sentence: 昨日のテストは酷い点でした。
notes: Usually written in kana. Covers awful and cruel both, from the weather to what somebody said to you.

sentence_meaning: This package is heavy.
mnemonic: The weight runs straight down the middle of the character and out the bottom. You get the case off the floor and regret every decision that led to it: おもい.
notes: Same sound as 思い おもい, a thought. Also does serious: 重い病気 おもいびょうき is a grave illness.
sentence: この荷物は重いですね。

notes: The 起 family: 起きる happens and also gets you up, 起こす causes it or wakes somebody, 起こる only ever happens. One vowel from 怒る おこる, to get angry.
sentence: この道ではよく事故が起こります。
mnemonic: 走 running with 己 yourself behind it, standing up out of nothing at all. Nobody caused this one and nobody is waking anybody: it simply happened. おこる.
sentence_meaning: There are many accidents on this road.

mnemonic: 辶 a road with a figure drawn upside down walking along it, against everything coming the other way. Whatever you assumed, the other way round: ぎゃく.
sentence_meaning: The station is in the opposite direction.
sentence: 駅は逆方向です。
notes: 逆に means conversely, or on the contrary. As a noun it is the opposite of the thing.

mnemonic: 糸 thread taking something in and stowing it, with 得 a hand coming back holding the prize. Not agreement. The point where the knot took and you stopped arguing: なっとく.
sentence_meaning: I was able to accept his explanation.
sentence: 彼の説明で納得できました。
notes: 納得する is being satisfied by an explanation. 賛成 さんせい is agreeing with the proposal itself.
楽しい たのしい is the feeling. 楽しむ is doing a thing for the pleasure of it.
sentence: 今日は一人の時間を楽しみたい。
mnemonic: The same 楽 as 楽しい, strings stretched across a wooden frame. Except this is not how it felt. This is what you did: sat down and took the whole afternoon: たのしむ.
sentence_meaning: Today I would like to enjoy some alone time.

meaning: to shout, to yell, to cry out
mnemonic: 口 a mouth with something twisted alongside it, and out it comes. Not aimed at anybody in particular, and the sake had a hand in it: さけぶ.
sentence_meaning: She cried out for help.
notes: 叫び声 さけびごえ is a scream. It is the noise rather than the message.
sentence: 彼女は助けを求めて大声で叫んだの。

mnemonic: 隹 a small bird on 木 a tree, then another, then the whole hedge is birds. Nobody organised it, nobody is in charge, and nobody is leaving: あつまる.
sentence_meaning: Lots of people are gathered in front of the station.
sentence: 駅前に人が集まっています。
notes: 集める あつめる is you gathering them up. 集まる is them gathering by themselves.

sentence: 子供に構いすぎてはいけない。
notes: 構わない is the form you meet first: I do not mind, do not trouble yourself. Same 構 as 結構 けっこう.
mnemonic: 木 timber put together into a frame, which is effort somebody chose to spend. Spend it on a person, or say 構わない and decline to: かまう.
sentence_meaning: You shouldn't give kids too much attention.
I visited the royal grave.
mnemonic: Three horizontal lines and one stroke joining them, and the man who claims to be the join. On his own, a king. Against another character, usually a jewel: おう.
sentence: 王の墓を見学したよ。
notes: The same shape on the left of another character is normally 玉 jewel with its dot worn off, which is why 理 and 現 have jewels in them.

sentence_meaning: Let's take a rest on the way for about 30 minutes.
mnemonic: 辶 a road with 余 whatever is left of it, and 中 the middle of that. Not arrived, not turned back. On the platform with the bag, chewing on another hour: とちゅう.
sentence: 途中で30分ほど休みましょう。
notes: 途中で is halfway through doing something. It covers distance and time both.

mnemonic: 忄 a heart with the same thing run through it again and again. The commute was unbearable in March and by June you are reading a book on it: なれる.
sentence_meaning: Have you gotten used to the new house yet?
notes: に marks what you get used to: 仕事に慣れる. 慣れ なれ on its own is the habit.
sentence: 新しい家にはもう慣れましたか。

notes: 終わる おわる is ending. 終わり is the end as a thing you can point at.
sentence: 今月の終わりに国へ帰ります。
sentence_meaning: I will return to my country at the end of this month.
mnemonic: 終わる stopped just short of being a verb. Not the ending. The point itself, the line drawn on the floor, and everybody already has their coat on: おわり.

meaning: for the time being, more or less
sentence_meaning: It might be better to just let him know for now.
mnemonic: 一 one and 応 a heart answering from under a shelter. One answer, given for now, with everything still unsaid sitting behind it: いちおう.
notes: Hedges whatever follows: more or less, for now, in principle. Often the speaker has reservations they are not going to state.
sentence: 彼にも一応知らせておいたほうがいいだろう。

notes: Very wide. Drawing a card, looking a word up, and 風邪を引く, catching a cold. Later comes 弾く ひく, playing a string instrument.
sentence: このドアは引いてください。
sentence_meaning: Please pull this door open.
mnemonic: 弓 a bow, and the line beside it is the string coming back. Pull a card, pull a muscle, pull the door marked push: ひく.

sentence: 海は広くて大きい。
notes: 海 うみ is the sea. In compounds it reads かい: 海外 かいがい is overseas.
sentence_meaning: The sea is vast and wide.
mnemonic: 氵 water with 毎 every alongside it. Every drop there is, all in one place, and it does not stop at the horizon: うみ.

sentence_meaning: You mustn't give up on everything so easily.
mnemonic: You put the pen down and say it to the room, and 言 is sat there on the left because this does not count until somebody has heard it: あきらめる.
notes: 諦めないで is do not give up. It is abandoning the attempt rather than losing.
sentence: 何でも簡単に諦めてはいけません。

mnemonic: 必 the heart with something run right through the middle of it, same as in 必要. No exceptions, no discussion. It will happen and you arrange the rest around it: かならず.
sentence_meaning: Always wear your seat belt.
sentence: 必ずシートベルトを着けてください。
notes: Stronger than きっと. 必ず is a guarantee; きっと is confidence.
Aiming a weapon, and equally going after a job or a prize.
sentence: 来年は優勝を狙います。
mnemonic: 犭 a beast flattened into the grass, and every part of it pointed at one thing out in the field. It decided some time ago: ねらう.
sentence_meaning: We will aim for a victory next year.

notes: いくらですか is how much is it. いくら〜ても is a different pattern altogether, meaning no matter how much.
sentence: この靴はいくらですか。
mnemonic: The tag has been turned over twice and there is still no number on it. Somebody is going to have to ask, and the somebody is you: いくら.
sentence_meaning: How much are these shoes?

mnemonic: 艹 grass and 氵 water on their way down, the same as 落ちる, except this time a hand let go. Phone, step, pavement: oh, toss. おとす.
sentence_meaning: I dropped my smartphone on the street.
notes: 落ちる おちる is it falling. 落とす is you dropping it, and it also covers losing something.
sentence: 道でスマホを落としました。
この部分は問題ないです。
notes: 全部 ぜんぶ is all of it; 部分 is a portion of it.
mnemonic: 部 one section of a thing with 分 a blade splitting it, so a part of a part. Not the whole essay. The paragraph somebody has underlined twice: ぶぶん.
sentence_meaning: There's no problem with this part.

mnemonic: 必 a heart with a stroke through it and 死 bare bones alongside. Certain death, used as an adverb. He asked the way you ask when there is no second go: ひっし.
sentence_meaning: Students are desperately trying to follow the class.
notes: 必死に is desperately or frantically. Literally certain death, which is about the tone of it.
sentence: 学生たちは授業についていくのに必死です。

notes: Also does unusual for you, as a compliment or a dig: 珍しいね, you are never normally here.
sentence: こんな大きなダイヤは珍しいです。
mnemonic: That 王 is the jewel one, not the king, the same as it is in 理. Snow in May, and every person on the street has stopped with a phone up: めずらしい.
sentence_meaning: A diamond big like this is rare.

notes: Same reading as 以外 いがい, except for. 意外 is a surprise, 以外 is an exclusion, and only the kanji separates them.
sentence: 意外にも彼は独身です。
sentence_meaning: Surprisingly, he is single.
mnemonic: 意 a sound landing on 心 a heart, and 外 everything outside. What happened was outside the part your mind had set aside room for: いがい.
報 a hand passing the news along, and 告 牛 a cow announced by 口 a mouth. Not the news. The written version somebody has to sign at the bottom: ほうこく.
sentence_meaning: There's a report about yesterday's conference.
notes: 報告する is to report. Same 報 as 情報 じょうほう.
sentence: 昨日の会議について報告があります。

mnemonic: 扌 a hand on the left, closing and not opening again. The same grip that shapes a nigiri, rice pressed into form by the fist alone: にぎる.
sentence_meaning: The girl clasped her mother's hand.
sentence: 少女は母親の手を握った。
notes: 握手 あくしゅ is a handshake, and おにぎり the rice ball comes from this verb.

mnemonic: 糸 a thread pulled into 吉 a lucky knot, and 婚 a woman at dusk, which is when it was done. The knot is the whole idea, and every language has it: けっこん.
sentence_meaning: My older sister is getting married next month.
sentence: 来月、姉が結婚します。
notes: 結婚する is to get married. Same 結 as 結果 けっか and 結構 けっこう.
戦う たたかう is to fight. 戦い is the fight as a noun, and 戦争 せんそう is a war.
sentence: 長い戦いが終わった。
sentence_meaning: The long battle came to an end.
mnemonic: 戦う stopped just short of being a verb. Not the fighting. The thing itself, with a name and a date and a field somebody can point at: たたかい.
咸 all of it landing on 心 a heart, and 謝 words loosed like an arrow. Not thanks said on the way out of the door. The kind you sit down and write: かんしゃ.
sentence_meaning: I am always thankful to my friends.
sentence: 友達にいつも感謝しています。
notes: 感謝する is to be grateful. ありがとう is the everyday version.
Rain, arguments, exercise, competition. Anything carrying more force than it needs.
sentence: 激しい雨が降っています。
sentence_meaning: A very heavy rain is falling.
mnemonic: 氵 water thrown hard at something rather than running past it. The argument did not build up to anything. It arrived at that volume and stayed there: はげしい.

notes: 倒す たおす is you knocking it down. 倒れる is it going over, and of a person it means collapsing.
sentence: 地震で家が倒れました。
sentence_meaning: The house collapsed from the earthquake.
mnemonic: 亻 a person arriving on the floor, and this time nobody put them there. He was fine at the table and then he was not, and the chair went with him: たおれる.

sentence_meaning: Everyone already knows that.
mnemonic: A figure already turning away from the bowl, done with it. Whatever you were about to suggest has happened, and there is nothing left to decide: すでに.
notes: Written and formal. もう is the everyday already.
sentence: そのことは既にみんな知っています。

mnemonic: 疒 the sickness radical wrapped round 皮 skin. Not ill. Worn through to the outside layer, and the stairs have opinions about it now: つかれる.
sentence_meaning: I'm tired and feel dizzy.
notes: お疲れ様 おつかれさま is said to somebody who has been working, and it is nearer to well done than to you look tired.
sentence: 私は疲れてふらふらです。

mnemonic: 生 a shoot pushing up, and 活 氵 water with 舌 a tongue in it, both of them alive. Not being alive. How you go about it, day after day: せいかつ.
sentence_meaning: Life in Japan is hard but also really fun.
sentence: 日本の生活は大変ですが、とても楽しいです。
notes: 命 いのち is life itself; 生活 is how it gets lived. 生活費 せいかつひ is living costs.

sentence: この場でお礼を言わせてください。
notes: 場所 ばしょ is the physical place. 場 alone leans towards the occasion: その場で, on the spot.
sentence_meaning: Please let me take this opportunity to offer my gratitude.
mnemonic: 土 earth with the sun coming up over it, the same 場 as 場所. On its own it thins out: not the address, the occasion, and the room it happened in: ば.

sentence: 私は家族を愛しています。
notes: Heavier and far more written than 好き. 愛 あい on its own is love as a noun.
sentence_meaning: I love my family.
mnemonic: 愛 a heart carried about in the middle of the character, with する bolted on to make it a thing you do. Not a feeling you have. A thing you keep choosing: あいする.
冫 the ice marks again, and whatever they touch goes the same way. The tap runs and your hand is off it before you decided to move: つめたい.
sentence_meaning: I want to drink cold juice.
sentence: 冷たいジュースが飲みたいです。
notes: Cold to the touch, and also cold in manner. 寒い さむい is cold weather.

sentence: この野菜は捨てないでください。
notes: 捨てる is discarding on purpose. 落とす おとす is dropping by accident, which is the difference that matters.
sentence_meaning: Please don't throw these vegetables away.
mnemonic: 扌 a hand on the left, opening. Everything else in the character is what it was holding until a second ago: すてる.

sentence_meaning: I want to spend my time living leisurely in a warm country.
mnemonic: 辶 the road, and where 過ぎる is time going past you, this is you doing something with it. A whole Sunday, and you chose every hour of it: すごす.
notes: 過ぎる すぎる is time passing. 過ごす is you passing it, deliberately.
sentence: 暖かい国でゆっくり過ごしたいです。
来週みんなで食事しましょう。
notes: 食事する is to have a meal. ご飯 ごはん is the everyday word for it.
mnemonic: 食 a lid over a heaped dish and 事 a matter being conducted. Not the food. The event: everybody sat down at once with the phones face down: しょくじ.
sentence_meaning: Let's have a meal with everyone next week.

mnemonic: 亻 a person with 動 movement bolted onto them, which is the whole of the idea. Coat on the hook, hat on the rack, and eight hours of it: はたらく.
sentence_meaning: My big sister works at a bank.
sentence: 姉は銀行で働いています。
notes: 仕事 しごと is the job. 働く is the doing of it. 働き者 はたらきもの is a hard worker.
答える こたえる is answering. 答え is the answer itself.
sentence: 答えが分かりません。
sentence_meaning: I don't know the answer.
mnemonic: 竹 bamboo strips with 合 the matching half fitted against them, and this is the half that fits rather than the fitting of it. It was on the board all along: こたえ.
The frame is the gust, and 虫 the insect inside it is what the old idea reckoned the wind was carrying. It comes round the building and takes your hat: かぜ.
sentence_meaning: The wind is strong today.
notes: 風邪 かぜ, with a different second character, is a cold. 風邪を引く かぜをひく is catching one.
sentence: 今日は風が強いです。

notes: 黒 くろ is the colour as a noun. Same 黒 as 黙る だまる, where it sits over a dog.
sentence: 彼女は黒いドレスを着ています。
sentence_meaning: She's wearing a black dress.
mnemonic: Soot in the window with 灬 fire underneath, which is where soot comes from. The crow on the fence is that colour all over, beak included: くろい.

sentence: 彼はシートベルトをしていたので助かったんだ。
notes: 助ける たすける is you helping. 助かる is being helped, and 助かった is what you say when it works out.
sentence_meaning: He survived because he was wearing a seat belt.
mnemonic: 力 power on the right, an extra shoulder under the load, the same as 助ける. Except this time it is your load and somebody else's shoulder: たすかる.

sentence: 彼からメールを受け取りました。
notes: Both halves are already in the deck. It also covers taking a remark a certain way: 悪く受け取る.
sentence_meaning: I got an email from him.
mnemonic: 受ける taking what comes and 取る closing a hand round it, welded together. Not simply that it arrived. You have it, and you have signed for it: うけとる.
meaning: to receive, to take (someone's words or behavior)

notes: 足りない is the form you meet more often, meaning not enough. 十分 じゅうぶん is having plenty.
sentence: お金がちょっと足りません。
meaning: to be enough, to be sufficient
mnemonic: 口 a knee over the foot below it, the same 足 as your leg. Here it is about reach: whether what you have gets you as far as the line. It does not: たりる.
sentence_meaning: There's not quite enough money.
His judgment is correct.
mnemonic: 刂 a blade telling two things apart, and 断 an axe taking one of them off for good. Both halves are somebody deciding, and neither of them is reversible: はんだん.
notes: 判断する is to judge or to decide. 決める きめる is picking; 判断 is the weighing that comes first.
sentence: 彼の判断は正しい。

mnemonic: 未 a tree with the top branch not out yet, and 来 the crop that has not come in. Nothing here has happened, which is the entire point of it: みらい.
sentence_meaning: Nobody knows the future.
notes: 未 means not yet, and turns up in 未定 みてい, undecided. 将来 しょうらい is your own future rather than the world's.
sentence: 未来は誰にも分からない。
腹一杯食った。
notes: Blunt and masculine. 食べる たべる is the neutral one. 食う also does living on something: 芸で食う.
sentence_meaning: I ate heartily.
mnemonic: The same 食 as 食べる, a lid over a heaped dish, except nobody here is being delicate about it. He eats standing up over the sink: くう.

sentence_meaning: This cake is your portion.
mnemonic: 八 splitting with 刀 a blade, so a portion cut off the whole. Your share of the bill, your share of the work, and the bun that comes with it: ぶん.
sentence: このケーキはあなたの分です。
notes: The portion belonging to something. 自分 じぶん is your own share, which is where the word for self comes from.
The casual form of そちら. こっち, そっち, あっち, どっち run exactly as これ, それ, あれ, どれ do.
sentence: そっちが私の部屋です。
mnemonic: そ- is your side of things again, and this is the offhand way of pointing at it. Not over there. Where you are, and nobody is reaching for こちら: そっち.
sentence_meaning: That's my room over there.
He's good at soccer and baseball.
mnemonic: 上 above the line and 手 a hand, so a hand above everybody else's. He makes it look like nothing at all, and you may as well not have tried: うまい.
sentence: 彼はサッカーも野球もとても上手いです。
notes: Also means tasty. 上手 じょうず is the same two characters read differently, and is the politer word for skilled.

sentence: 日時はご都合に合わせます。
notes: 合う あう is things matching by themselves. 合わせる is you making them match.
sentence_meaning: The date can be scheduled according to your circumstances.
mnemonic: 𠆢 a lid coming down onto 口 a mouth, the same as 合う, except this time somebody is doing the fitting. Watches set to the same minute before anyone leaves: あわせる.
大 big and 切 a blade, which reads wrong until you think of cutting a thing out in order to keep it. Tie it, set it aside, let nobody else near: たいせつ.
sentence_meaning: This is a ring that meant a lot to my mother.
sentence: これは母が大切にしていた指輪です。
notes: 大事 だいじ is the near twin and either does most of the time. 大切にする is to treasure something.

mnemonic: 艹 grass on top, and underneath it something caught halfway through turning. One stem in a jar and the whole room is different: はな.
sentence_meaning: My mother likes flowers.
sentence: 母は花が好きです。
notes: Later comes 鼻 はな, nose, which sounds identical. 花見 はなみ is flower viewing.

mnemonic: 言 speech with an arrow loosed beside it, the same 謝 as 感謝. Words sent out on purpose, except this time sending them costs you something: あやまる.
sentence_meaning: Be sure to apologize when you've done something wrong.
sentence: 自分が悪い時は謝りましょう。
notes: Same 謝 as 感謝 かんしゃ. Both are words you have to actually put out there.

sentence: その男は彼女のバッグを奪ったぞ。
notes: Taking by force. 取る とる is neutral, and 盗む ぬすむ is stealing quietly.
sentence_meaning: That man stole her bag.
mnemonic: The bird was in somebody else's hand a moment ago, and the big figure standing over it did not ask. It is his now: うばう.
meaning: to snatch, to take by force

sentence: そのチームには勢いがありますね。
notes: 勢いで means on a roll, carried by it. 力 ちから is strength standing still.
mnemonic: 力 power at the bottom and everything above it stacking up. Once it is moving nobody needs to push any more, and nobody could stop it either: いきおい.
sentence_meaning: That team has momentum.

notes: 涙が出る なみだがでる is the usual way of saying you are crying. 泣く なく is the act itself.
sentence: 動物の映画を見て、涙が出ました。
mnemonic: 氵 water with 戻 returning beside it, because it comes back whether you want it to or not. She got through the whole speech and then the last line went: なみだ.
sentence_meaning: I saw a movie about animals and cried.

mnemonic: 雨 rain split into 分 parts, 囲 a border drawn round it, and 気 the steam of the place. Three characters for a thing nobody can point at. It was fun, then it went icky: ふんいき.
sentence_meaning: The shop has a really good atmosphere.
notes: The feel of a place or a moment. 空気 くうき does the same job in 空気を読む, reading the room.
sentence: とても雰囲気のいいお店ですね。

mnemonic: 口 a mouth on the left with nothing whatsoever beside it. Sound coming out with no substance behind it, which is the whole definition: うそ.
sentence_meaning: It's not a lie. It's true.
notes: 嘘つき うそつき is a liar. 嘘! on its own is you are kidding.
sentence: 嘘じゃありません。本当です。

mnemonic: 月 the moon down in the corner, and the whole rest of the character is the distance to it. Wanting a thing you cannot reach from here, and no amount of zoom helps: のぞむ.
sentence_meaning: He hopes to marry me.
notes: 希望 きぼう is hope as a noun. 望む is the wanting itself.
sentence: 彼は私との結婚を望んでいます。

sentence_meaning: I was really nervous during my speech yesterday.
mnemonic: 糸 thread pulled until it will not give, and 張 a bow drawn 長 long. Two things at full stretch. Stood up to speak and your voice has gone elsewhere: きんちょう.
sentence: 昨日のスピーチはとても緊張しました。
notes: 緊張する is to be nervous. Same 張 as 頑張る がんばる, where the stretch is effort rather than nerves.

sentence_meaning: Do you want to eat together?
mnemonic: 一 one and 緒 a thread with a person on the end of it. Two of you tied into a single strand, going the same way whether or not it was agreed: いっしょ.
sentence: 一緒に食事しよっか。
notes: 一緒に is together as an adverb. It also means the same: 一緒だ, they are identical.

sentence: 彼女は通りがかりの人に救われたよ。
notes: 助ける たすける is helping, up to and including rescue. 救う is the rescue itself, and heavier.
mnemonic: 求 seeking with 攵 a hand striking alongside, so going in and getting somebody out. Straight off the bank and scooped the dog up with one arm: すくう.
sentence_meaning: She was saved by a passing stranger.
The president himself negotiated with that company.
mnemonic: 自 the nose you point at to mean me, the same as in 自分. Except this one is an adverb: nobody asked him, nobody sent him, he went: みずから.
sentence: 社長自らがその会社と交渉したよ。
notes: Formal and written. 自分で じぶんで is the everyday by myself.

sentence: 地面に何か絵が描いてあるぞ。
notes: 地 reads ち on its own meaning ground, and じ in compounds like this one.
sentence_meaning: There is some kind of picture drawn on the ground.
mnemonic: 土 earth on the left and 面 the face of a thing. Not the soil and not the planet. The flat top of it, which is what you land on: じめん.

sentence: 一度の失敗であきらめてはいけないよ。
notes: 失敗する is to fail or to make a mistake. 成功 せいこう is succeeding.
sentence_meaning: You must not give up after one blunder.
mnemonic: 失 a hand letting go without meaning to, and 敗 money with a hand striking at it. You lost hold and it cost something, and everybody saw: しっぱい.
辶 the road again, except this one takes the long way on purpose. He saw them at the far end of the aisle and found something urgent in the other direction: さける.
